Admins gain expanded conditions and condition combinations, multiple activities per rule, simulation mode, configurable alerts and notifications, and rule match activities become visible in activity explorer. Roadmap status is In development, on Web, with release phases General Availability and Preview. On 6 October 2026 the roadmap release date moved from January 2027 to March 2027; it had moved from December 2026 to January 2027 on 16 September.
items.why: Directly relevant: it ties DLP inline protection to an Entra Conditional Access grant control and surfaces rule matches in activity explorer, giving identity admins a new enforcement lever and detection engineers a new telemetry source.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft.
items.fingerprintBefore: Microsoft Purview is upgrading inline data protection for Microsoft Entra-managed apps in Edge for Business, integrating with a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access grant control and simplifying configuration while removing current Purview policy restrictions. Admins gain expanded conditions and condition combinations, multiple activities per rule, simulation mode, configurable alerts and notifications, and rule match activities become visible in activity explorer. Roadmap status is In development, on Web, with release phases General Availability and Preview.

items.title: Passkey or passwordless sign-in as the first MFA method: phase 1 slips to late October and its completion to late November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method
items.tier0Note: Registration is where an account's authentication strength is decided for the rest of its life.
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 7 August 2026, revised on 8 October 2026: 'Updated October 8, 2026: We have updated the timeline.' Phase 1, synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows and FIDO2 security keys: 'We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 (previously early October) and expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November).' Phase 2, Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, Authenticator app passkey and Authenticator passwordless sign-in, is unchanged and still reads 'early January 2026' to 'late February 2027' as Microsoft prints it. Confirm in your own tenant.
items.why: A password-only user will be able to register a passkey with no earlier MFA method on the account. Microsoft's own recommendation in the post is to 'Consider requiring MFA to register security information if additional verification is required by your organization.' The change now reaches tenants about three weeks later than this page said.
items.action: Move the re-baselining of registration-event alerting from early to late October, and review the Conditional Access policy on the 'Register security information' user action before the rollout reaches the tenant.
items.dateNote: First published by Microsoft on 7 Aug 2026; the row is inside the 24 September to 8 October period because Microsoft revised the post on 8 Oct 2026.

items.title: Managed identity for host pools reaches GA, and a future update will require it
items.officialTitle: Managed identity support
items.tier0Note: A host pool that cannot add session hosts cannot scale out, and the requirement is announced but not dated.
items.fingerprint: September 2026, GA: managed identity support for host pools, with Microsoft stating that a future service update will require a managed identity to add session hosts to host pools configured with session host configuration. No date is stated by Microsoft.
items.why: The requirement is announced without a date, so the only safe assumption is that it lands before anyone re-reads the page.
items.action: Assign managed identities to host pools using session host configuration now, rather than waiting for the date.

items.title: The AD FS Risky IP report is deprecated in favour of the Risky IP workbook
items.officialTitle: Risky IP report (AD FS)
items.tier0Note: This report is how password-spray against AD FS gets noticed at all.
items.fingerprint: Documentation note dated 18 September 2026: the AD FS version of the Risky IP report is being deprecated and Microsoft directs readers to the Risky IP workbook instead.
items.why: A deprecated report keeps rendering until it does not, and the workbook is a different artefact with different plumbing.
items.action: Rebuild any AD FS password-spray monitoring on the Risky IP workbook before the report stops.

items.title: Access drift reporting arrives in preview for groups and enterprise applications
items.officialTitle: Entitlement Management Access Drift Reporting
items.tier0Note: Drifted access is standing access nobody reviews, which is what an attacker inherits with the account.
items.fingerprint: 18 September 2026, public preview: drift reports for groups and enterprise applications, requiring an Identity Governance or Entra Suite licence, alongside a new reconciliation overview defining access drift, account discovery and enforcement.
items.why: It names unmanaged and orphaned access as a reportable condition rather than something an audit has to reconstruct.
items.action: Run the drift report over the groups that grant privileged access and treat the output as a review queue.

items.title: Global Secure Access allows up to ten custom Private Access forwarding profiles, and priority decides which one applies
items.officialTitle: Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles
items.tier0Note: A forwarding profile decides which users reach which private applications, so its priority is an access control.
items.fingerprint: Tenants can create custom Private Access traffic forwarding profiles in addition to the single default one, up to ten during preview. Each custom profile carries its own acquisition rules, assignments, status and priority, and profiles can be assigned to users, groups, devices and device platforms, with nested group membership supported. When several enabled profiles for the same traffic type apply to a user and device, only the applicable profile with the highest priority is used. Deleted custom profiles cannot be restored.
items.why: Priority is now the thing that decides who reaches which private application, and priority is a field rather than an assignment. A change to it re-scopes access without any assignment changing, which is invisible to a review that reads assignments only.
items.action: Add create, modify and delete of traffic forwarding profiles to Global Secure Access audit log monitoring, and treat a priority change as an access change in review. The stated use case — excluding privileged applications from a broadly assigned profile — is worth building deliberately rather than inheriting.

items.title: Windows devices re-evaluate compliance on a security state change instead of waiting for check-in
items.officialTitle: Faster compliance updates for Windows devices
items.tier0Note: Compliance state is an input to device-based Conditional Access, so its latency is an access-control latency.
items.fingerprint: Week of 14 September 2026: client-driven compliance evaluation lets a Windows device trigger re-evaluation when firewall, antivirus, BitLocker, Defender status, OS build, real-time protection or Secure Boot state changes, rather than waiting for the scheduled check-in.
items.why: It shortens the gap between a host losing a security control and Conditional Access knowing about it.
items.action: Expect compliance events to arrive sooner and re-check any alert threshold tuned to the old check-in cadence.

items.title: The v3.x sensor covers AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect, by manual activation only
items.officialTitle: Sensor v3.x support for additional identity server roles: AD CS, AD FS, and Entra Connect
items.tier0Note: AD CS and AD FS are the two servers that mint credentials for the whole forest.
items.fingerprint: September 2026, preview: sensor v3.x extends to AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers through manual activation; Microsoft states automatic activation and migration are not yet supported for these roles.
items.why: Certificate services and federation are the highest-value identity servers and the ones a domain-controller-only sensor plan misses.
items.action: Activate the sensor manually on AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers; do not wait for automatic activation, which Microsoft says does not cover them.

items.title: The v3.x sensor can be activated on a domain controller without onboarding Defender for Endpoint first
items.officialTitle: Sensor v3.x onboarding without Microsoft Defender for Endpoint deployment
items.tier0Note: Domain controller coverage is the difference between seeing an identity attack and reading about it afterwards.
items.fingerprint: September 2026, preview: the MDI sensor v3.x can be activated on eligible domain controllers running Windows Server 2019 or later without first onboarding the server to Defender for Endpoint.
items.why: MDE onboarding was the step that stalled MDI coverage on domain controllers nobody wanted to touch.
items.action: Re-check which domain controllers were left without a sensor because of the MDE prerequisite.

items.title: Windows App adds three client-side wildcard domains for Windows 365
items.officialTitle: Action required: Allow new Windows App client-side endpoints for Windows 365
items.fingerprint: From early October 2026 Windows App uses *.windows.cloud.microsoft, *.service.windows.cloud.microsoft and *.windows.static.microsoft on 443/TCP for client-side traffic; firewall, proxy, VPN, DNS filtering and SWG policies must allow them or sign-in and connection fail.
items.action: Before Windows App starts using them in early October, allow outbound 443/TCP to *.windows.cloud.microsoft, *.service.windows.cloud.microsoft and *.windows.static.microsoft in firewall, proxy, VPN, DNS-filter and Secure Web Gateway policy for user devices, and check that TLS inspection does not break them.
items.why: This is a client-side allow-list change: a device behind a managed network boundary that does not allow the three wildcard domains fails to sign in or connect to its Cloud PC, and the failure looks like an outage rather than a policy block.

items.title: Admins get a control over who can upload advanced agents and plugins; uploads stay open by default from 25 Oct
items.officialTitle: Manage who can upload advanced agents and plugins
items.deadlineNote: 25 October 2026 is when advanced-package uploads become enabled by default unless an admin has chosen no users or specific users or groups.
items.fingerprint: From 25 September 2026 the Microsoft 365 admin center shows an Advanced package uploads setting under Copilot settings (all users, no users, or specific users or Entra ID groups). An advanced package is a declarative agent with actions or with an MCP server. Starting 25 October 2026 advanced-package uploads are enabled by default unless the admin has restricted them. Updated 15 September 2026.
items.why: User-uploaded agents with actions or MCP servers can reach data and external endpoints; the default after 25 October is open.
items.action: Decide before 25 October 2026 who may upload advanced agents and plugins, and scope the setting to an Entra ID group if not all users.

items.title: Microsoft withdraws the profile card change: the eleven properties stay hidden by default and the 31 October date is gone
items.officialTitle: Default visibility of additional profile card properties in Microsoft 365 profile cards
items.fingerprint: Published 24 July 2026, revised 22 September and again 7 October 2026. Microsoft added: 'Updated October 7, 2026: We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time. We apologize for any inconvenience.' The rollout line now reads 'General Availability (Worldwide): We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time.' where it gave late October 2026. The eleven properties were Division, Role, Employee number, Employee type, Cost center, User principal name, Alias, Fax, Street address, State and Postal code.
items.why: The data-exposure change with a date is off: directory attributes such as employee number, cost center and street address stay hidden on profile cards unless an administrator shows them. Microsoft writes 'at this time', so the change can return under a new post.
items.action: Stop the 31 October hide-before-rollout work. Keep any properties already hidden through the Graph profile card API as they are, and watch for a new Message Center post. Confirm in your own tenant.
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft withdrew the change on 7 October 2026, so the 31 October 2026 date this page carried no longer applies. The post's own action text still names October 31, 2026; Microsoft did not edit that paragraph.

items.title: (Updated) The September 2026 Windows non-security preview update is now available
items.officialTitle: (Updated) The September 2026 Windows non-security preview update is now available
items.deadlineNote: Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro editions reach end of support in October 2026.
items.fingerprint: The September 2026 non-security preview update is available for Windows 11 versions 26H1, 25H2 and 24H2, via KB5124006 (26H1) and KB5124010 (25H2 and 24H2); the 25H2 highlights include remapping the Copilot key to Right Ctrl or Context Menu, OneDrive camera roll backup in Settings, Emoji 17.0, File Explorer preview changes including a Preview anyway button for HTML files, and a new Open apps maximized setting. Microsoft added a note that KB5124010 is the final preview update for Windows 11, version 24H2; supported 24H2 editions keep receiving monthly security updates per their servicing lifecycle, and 24H2 Home and Pro reach end of support in October 2026. Microsoft also notes a limited number of devices might see one additional restart during installation after a Secure Boot certificate update is applied.
items.why: Relevant to patch and endpoint owners: 24H2 stops receiving non-security previews, its Home and Pro editions reach end of support in October 2026, and the Secure Boot certificate update can cause an extra reboot that may look anomalous in endpoint telemetry.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft.

items.title: Azure Blueprints stops accepting new assignments on 31 October, and its resource locks stop working at full retirement
items.officialTitle: Azure Blueprints retirement
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date on the retirement page; the timeline has been extended more than once since the original 2023 announcement.
items.deadlineNote: 31 Oct 2026 ends modification of blueprint definitions and creation of new assignments; 31 Dec 2026 ends modification of existing assignments; 31 Jan 2027 is full retirement, when the API stops responding and unexported content is permanently deleted.
items.fingerprint: Phased retirement. From 31 October 2026 existing blueprint definitions can no longer be modified and new blueprint assignments can no longer be created. From 31 December 2026 existing assignments can no longer be modified. On 31 January 2027 the API stops responding, the CLI and PowerShell commands stop, Blueprints is removed from the portal, and unexported definitions, versions and assignments are permanently deleted.
items.why: Blueprint assignments can apply Do Not Delete and Read Only locks. Those locks stop functioning at retirement, so any resource whose protection rests on a blueprint lock silently loses it — and the definitions that describe what was being protected are deleted at the same time.
items.action: Export every blueprint definition, version and assignment you intend to keep before 31 January 2027, and before 31 October decide the replacement for each lock: Azure Policy deny or denyAction for the rule, and a resource lock for the deletion protection.

items.deadlineNote: (inferred) Microsoft's 60-day reminder was published on 15 September 2026; 10 November 2026 is the November Patch Tuesday this brief reads that reminder against.
items.why: 23H2 is the fallback build most estates parked on while they qualified 24H2 — and 24H2 dies a month earlier.
items.action: Plan one upgrade, not two: any device on 23H2 or 24H2 needs to be on 25H2 or 26H1 before the November update.
items.title: Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education reach end of updates in November — 60 days out
items.officialTitle: 60-Day Reminder: Windows 11, version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions reach end of updates
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's 60-day reminder that Windows 11 version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions reach end of updates in November 2026.

items.title: Azure Functions in-process model loses support on 10 November 2026
items.officialTitle: Azure Functions In-process model end of support
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date for a lifecycle row; the page was last updated 19 August 2026.
items.fingerprint: The in-process model for .NET Azure Functions reaches end of support on 10 November 2026; workloads must move to the isolated worker model.

items.title: Defender for Cloud Apps file policies retire on 6 January 2027
items.officialTitle: File policies retiring January 6, 2027
items.fingerprint: Carried on the Defender for Cloud Apps release notes, whose newest entry is 4 September 2026: file policies retire on 6 January 2027.
items.why: File policies are where a lot of SaaS data-at-rest detection still lives.
items.action: Inventory active file policies and decide what replaces each one before January.

items.title: Entra applies a cross-origin opener policy across web protocols from 31 January 2027
items.officialTitle: Prepare apps for Microsoft Entra COOP policy
items.fingerprint: Recorded in the Entra documentation feed for 24 September 2026: new applications become subject to the Microsoft Entra cross-origin opener policy across web protocols after 31 January 2027.
items.why: A COOP policy breaks popup-based sign-in flows that rely on a handle to the opener window, which is how a lot of older single-page applications authenticate.
items.action: Test any application whose sign-in opens a popup and reads window.opener against the COOP behaviour well before 31 January 2027.

items.title: Microsoft Purview: DSPM-Copilot Readiness and Data Explorer
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: DSPM-Copilot Readiness and Data Explorer
items.fingerprint: Microsoft is introducing readiness for Microsoft Copilot and data explorer experiences in Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM). The Copilot readiness experience consolidates insights into sensitive data exposure, oversharing and protection coverage so security teams can identify risks and track progress toward a more secure Copilot deployment. The data explorer experience provides a centralized investigation surface bringing together sites, sensitive data and preset views, to understand where sensitive data exists across sites and review site-level access. Roadmap status is In development, on Web, with release phases General Availability and Preview.
items.why: Strongly relevant to data security teams: oversharing and sensitive-data exposure insights plus site-level access review are the core inputs for assessing Copilot data risk and prioritizing remediation.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft.

items.title: Outlook and Word remote code execution has its title and CVSS score changed twice inside the window
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Outlook and Word Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.fingerprint: Title updated 21 September 2026, then title and CVSS score updated again 25 September 2026, both marked informational by Microsoft.
items.why: A score that moves twice in five days means the priority a ticket was opened with is no longer the priority Microsoft states.
items.action: Re-read the current CVSS score before closing any deferral decision taken on the earlier one.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft published four near-identical posts on 14 September 2026 — MC1472023, MC1472022, MC1472021 and MC1472019 — covering calendar events and Wait-on-Send across Outlook Mobile and Outlook for Mac. They are carried here as one item.
items.why: Meeting bodies and attachments have been a DLP blind spot on exactly the clients people use away from a managed desktop. Closing it will also generate new DLP alert volume that has to be triaged rather than suppressed.
items.action: Warn the DLP triage queue before the rollout lands, and check that calendar-event matches are routed like mail matches rather than into an unread bucket.
items.title: Purview DLP starts inspecting Outlook calendar events on mobile and Mac
items.officialTitle: (Updated) [Outlook Mobile] Purview Data Loss Prevention support for Calendar Events
items.fingerprint: Purview Data Loss Prevention gains support for calendar events and for Wait-on-Send in Outlook Mobile and Outlook for Mac, published as four separate Message Center posts on 14 September 2026. Revised by Microsoft on 6 October 2026: general availability moved from late September to mid-November 2026.
items.revisedNote: Revised at source on 6 October 2026, found in the afternoon pass at 21:33 Warsaw.

items.title: Endpoint DLP stops raising an event per file inside an archive and raises one for the archive
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Archive file classification behavior change for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention on Windows endpoints
items.fingerprint: Published 18 September 2026. Preview late September to mid-October 2026, general availability late October to early November 2026. Windows endpoints only. Endpoint DLP changes how it classifies archive files: the behaviour moves from per-contained-file events to archive-level handling.
items.why: Any detection, report or DLP alert rule that counts individual file events inside a zip will see its counts change without anyone editing a policy.
items.action: Find the queries and reports that key on file-level endpoint DLP events inside archives and re-baseline them before the GA window in late October.

items.title: A SpaceXAI subprocessor setting appears in the admin center, off by default, unlocking Grok models in Office apps
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Copilot: SpaceXAI subprocessor admin setting
items.fingerprint: SpaceXAI joins Microsoft's Online Services Subprocessor List and a SpaceXAI setting appears under AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors in the Microsoft 365 admin center from 18 September 2026. It is disabled by default and only eligible Frontier customers see it; tenants in the EU, EFTA and the UK and all government clouds are excluded from the initial rollout. Enabled, it makes Grok models selectable in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, scoped to users or groups, under Microsoft's Product Terms and DPA. Microsoft states SOC 1 Type II, PCI, FedRAMP and HITRUST certifications are not currently available for SpaceXAI.
items.why: A third-party model provider becomes reachable from inside Office documents on an admin toggle. The default is off and no data is processed until someone turns it on, so the control is real — but the certification gap Microsoft names is the thing a compliance team has to rule on before anybody does.
items.action: Decide the answer before someone asks: review the subprocessor documentation and SpaceXAI's certification position, and record whether the setting stays off. If it goes on, scope it to a group rather than the tenant.

items.title: Browser Use Admin Control for Copilot Cowork
items.officialTitle: Browser Use Admin Control for Copilot Cowork
items.fingerprint: Controls for browser use in Copilot Cowork are now available in the Microsoft 365 admin center, with granular scoping so admins can enable the capability for no users, all users, or specific security groups rather than tenant-wide only. The setting is at Copilot > Settings > View All > Cowork settings, under "Allow browser access" ("Allow Cowork to use the Microsoft Edge browser to perform tasks on behalf of users"), and is disabled by default. General Availability rollout runs from mid-September 2026 to late September 2026 worldwide.
items.why: Directly security-relevant: this governs whether an AI agent may drive Microsoft Edge to act on a user's behalf, so identity and SOC teams should confirm the scope is deliberately set rather than broadly enabled.
items.action: Review which users or security groups should receive access and, if the capability is wanted, enable it under Copilot > Settings > View All > Cowork settings by selecting "Allow browser access", ideally starting with a small pilot group.

items.title: Remediation actions move into the Teams message entity flyout, closing the Teams triage-to-containment loop
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Remediation actions from the Teams message entity flyout
items.fingerprint: Analysts can trigger remediation actions directly from the Teams message entity flyout in Microsoft Defender for Office 365, rather than leaving the entity view for a separate remediation workflow. Rollout spans September and October 2026.
items.why: It pairs with the MessageContents advanced hunting table landing in the same weeks: the content is queryable in one place and the action is now available in the same pane, so the Teams phishing path is investigate-and-respond inside one portal.
items.action: Update the Teams phishing playbook to take the flyout action, and re-check who holds the remediation permission now that the action sits one click from triage.

items.title: EmailPostDeliveryEvents gains an ApproverUpn column naming who approved a remediation
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: View approver details for remediation actions in Advanced Hunting
items.fingerprint: An ApproverUpn column is added to the EmailPostDeliveryEvents table in Advanced Hunting, carrying the user principal name of whoever approved an eligible remediation action, for manual remediations and for AIR remediations that require approval. General availability worldwide including GCC, GCC High and DoD, enabled by default, no administrator action. Microsoft states nothing else about the table changes: no existing column, no permission, no approval workflow and no Action Center content is affected.
items.why: Who approved a remediation was previously only answerable in Action Center, one incident at a time. As a column it becomes joinable — approvals per analyst, approvals outside working hours, approvals on mail that was later found benign — and it makes an approval trail available to a detection rather than to a person clicking through.
items.action: Add ApproverUpn to the standing post-delivery remediation query and decide whether an approval by an unexpected principal, or outside a shift pattern, should raise anything.

items.title: WDS server role is deprecated in the next Windows Server release; hands-free PXE already off since April
items.officialTitle: Windows Deployment Services (WDS) deprecation in the next Windows Server release
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft names no date beyond “the next Windows Server release”.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft plans to deprecate the Windows Deployment Services server role — the inbox role, its services, management tools and interfaces, and WDS-provided PXE boot — beginning with the next Windows Server release. WDS hands-free deployment was already disabled by default and unsupported after the Windows updates of 14 April 2026, hardening guidance issued against CVE-2026-0386. Nothing changes on currently supported Windows Server releases.
items.why: PXE boot is an unauthenticated network service on the build VLAN; a deprecated one that stays switched on after April's hardening is an exposure item, not a platform footnote.
items.action: Inventory WDS deployments and their indirect dependencies, validate an alternative such as Configuration Manager operating-system deployment, and keep supported systems in place during the transition.

items.title: Copilot Memory becomes a retention target in Data Lifecycle Management
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management – Retention for Copilot Memory
items.fingerprint: Published 24 September 2026, rolling out late September to mid-October 2026. Retention policies can be applied to Copilot Memory, with eDiscovery and Exchange Online in scope. Microsoft states no immediate action is required before rollout.
items.why: Copilot Memory is a new store of user content. Until it is inside a retention policy it is neither preserved for an investigation nor deleted on a schedule.
items.action: Decide whether Copilot Memory falls under your existing retention requirement and check who holds the DLM admin permissions before the mid-October rollout completes.

items.title: Network data security policies no longer need a pay-as-you-go subscription
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview | DLP-Create Purview network data security policies without pay-as-you-go configuration
items.fingerprint: Published 24 September 2026 and revised 25 September 2026, rolling out late September to late October 2026. Network data security policies can be created over Entra Internet Access traffic without configuring pay-as-you-go billing first.
items.why: It removes the billing step that was keeping network-layer DLP over Global Secure Access traffic out of most tenants, which makes the network-layer DLP general availability announced on 16 September actually reachable.
items.action: Read the prerequisites and pilot one network data security policy over Internet Access traffic.

items.title: Outlook link previews are gone because the browser service that fetched them was deprecated; Microsoft now says why
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft Outlook: Link preview retirement
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 25 September 2026, revised 6 October 2026: 'We have updated the content.' Microsoft now states the reason: the Link Preview feature has been retired in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web 'because the browser service required to retrieve preview content from the web was deprecated. Without this, Outlook can no longer access the information needed to generate preview cards.' Links continue to function as standard clickable hyperlinks, and the change has already been implemented for Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD.
items.why: Marginal for security, though removing auto-generated preview cards means Outlook no longer fetches remote link metadata at compose time, one less automatic outbound request from the client.
items.action: No action is required; Microsoft recommends informing users that link preview cards will no longer be automatically generated when composing email.
items.fingerprintBefore: The link preview feature has been retired in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web, so Outlook no longer generates preview cards when users insert or paste web links into email messages. Links continue to function as standard clickable hyperlinks. Microsoft states the change has already been implemented for Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD.

items.title: Edge autolaunch on Windows startup becomes an opt-in a policy can pin three ways
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Edge: Autolaunch opt-in experience for managed devices
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Edge gains an opt-in experience letting users on managed devices choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts. Administrators can manage the behaviour with the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy, which takes opt-in, opt-out and user-choice configurations.
items.why: A browser that starts with the session changes what a stolen or unlocked device exposes, and the user-choice setting hands that decision to the user unless the policy is pinned. It is a one-line policy decision that is easier to make before the experience ships than after users have opted themselves in.
items.action: Set LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled explicitly in the Edge management service rather than leaving it at user choice, and note the setting in the managed-device baseline.

items.title: The endpoint map catches up with the 24 September permissions sync: three permissions, three more endpoints
items.fingerprint: The graphMap in the state block was still built from c1d06c5, the 22 September Weekly Permissions sync, while the catalog already carried the three endpoint additions Microsoft published on 24 September. Rebuilt in this run from 274c9b9: 24,164 method-and-path pairs over 7,459 paths, up from 24,161 over 7,457. ChannelSettings.ReadWrite.All gains POST /teams/{id}/deletedchannels/{id}/restore; SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All each gain GET /security/collaboration/verdictStatuses/{id}.
items.why: An already-consented permission reaching a new endpoint raises no consent prompt, so the map is the only place the widening shows. A map a day behind its source answers yesterday's question.
items.action: Nothing in the tenant. In the Graph API tab, those three permissions now list the new endpoints under What this permission can call.
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no titled post for this finding; it was measured in this run and the title above is this brief's own.

items.title: IdentityRiskEvent.ReadWrite.All gains a delegated scheme and an agent-notification endpoint
items.officialTitle: IdentityRiskEvent.ReadWrite.All
items.fingerprint: In the 25 September sync the permission changed from application-only to carrying a DelegatedWork scheme as well, and its published wording moved from “Read and write all risk detection information” to “Read and write identity risk event information”. Both IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All and IdentityRiskEvent.ReadWrite.All also gained the endpoint /identityProtection/settings/agentNotifications.
items.why: Write access to Identity Protection risk state is how an attacker dismisses their own risk detection; the scheme going delegated widens who can hold it.
items.action: Re-run your consent review for IdentityRiskEvent.ReadWrite.All: a delegated scheme means a signed-in user's app can now update risk state, which application-only consent reporting would not have shown.

items.title: Policies and apps can be rolled out in rings with approval gates through deployment plans
items.officialTitle: Stage app and policy rollout with deployment plans
items.fingerprint: Week of 21 September 2026: a Deployments experience for staged rollout across rings with Multiple Admin Approval integration, covering Windows and Win32 and Enterprise App Catalog apps, Settings Catalog policies and Endpoint Security policies.
items.why: Endpoint security policy is the change most able to lock a fleet out of its own network, and this is the blast-radius control for it.
items.action: Move endpoint security and Settings Catalog rollouts onto deployment plans with approval gates.

items.title: The Message Center index is now read whole — 2,497 rows in one request — and its date column turns out to be Last updated, not Published
items.reference: no MC/RM post — measured in this run
items.fingerprint: mc.merill.net renders 'Showing 200 of 2497 results' in its table but embeds the whole result set in the page payload: 2,497 rows, 712 Message Center and 1,785 Roadmap, read in one request in this pass instead of the 200 rows previous passes took from the table. Measured against twelve message pages: the index column is Last updated, not Published — MC1251206 carries 22 September 2026 in the index and 13 March 2026 on its own page, and five of the twelve differ the same way.
items.why: Reading the table gave a slice reaching back nine days, so an entry Microsoft revised inside the window but first published months ago never entered the comparison. That is precisely the class of miss the revision sweep exists to catch, and with DeltaPulse absent it is now the only way to catch it.
items.action: Nothing in the tenant. In this brief the published date now comes from each message page and the index date is carried as revisedOn; every comparison is recorded in the date audit in the Sources tab.
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no titled post for this finding; it was measured in this run and the title above is this brief's own.

items.title: Microsoft publishes Storm-2570's repeated tradecraft across deployments, not just its ransomware payload

The first stage is now called Public Preview and begins late October 2026 (previously Targeted Release, late September); General Availability begins late November 2026 (previously late October). The setting Collect agent observability data stays the administrator's control.
items.why: Agent 365 reads the third-party platform with the credentials the connection already holds, so the reach of an existing service connection grows without anyone re-consenting to it. The setting is off for connections that already exist and on by default for every connection made from now on, which means the default changes quietly under whoever creates the next one.
items.action: Before the next connection is created, decide whether agent telemetry from AWS, Google and Anthropic should land in Agent 365 at all, and write that decision down. Clear Collect agent observability data during setup where it should not. Check what the connection credential can already read on the source side: Bedrock Classic needs S3 trace read, AgentCore needs CloudWatch log query, Vertex AI needs BigQuery, Monitoring and Cloud Trace roles. Third-party providers may bill for the tracing and query these reads generate.
items.fingerprintBefore: Microsoft Agent 365 brings activity from Amazon Bedrock Classic and AgentCore, Google Vertex AI and Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview) into the same observability experience as Microsoft agents; runs, sessions, tool calls and exceptions appear on each synchronised agent's Activity tab. Collection stays disabled on existing connections until an administrator enables it, and the new Collect agent observability data setting is enabled by default for new connections.

items.title: The SharePoint mobile app is rebuilt around a personalised Discover home, and the app stops taking its branding from the Microsoft 365 admin center
items.officialTitle: New SharePoint Mobile Experience on iOS and Android
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states General Availability worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD beginning and completing mid-October 2026, and sets no action date.
items.fingerprint: The SharePoint mobile app for iOS and Android is redesigned around the personalised SharePoint Discover experience, with site browsing, in-app previews of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, image and video files, refreshed news and search, deep linking and dark mode. Following is renamed Favorites. iOS first, then Android. Microsoft states no admin action is needed and no compliance considerations.
items.why: A redesigned home that surfaces files, sites, people and news it judges relevant changes what an unlocked phone shows at a glance, and in-app preview of Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF means content is rendered inside the SharePoint app rather than handed to the app whose protection policy you wrote. The branding change also removes a visual cue users were told to trust.
items.action: Check that the app protection policy covering the SharePoint app on iOS and Android still covers the in-app preview path, since files are now previewed inside SharePoint rather than opened in Word, Excel or PowerPoint. Tell the service desk that Following is now Favorites before mid-October, so the rename does not arrive as a fault report.

items.title: New Viva Engage communities subscribe every member to community email and calendar invitations by default
items.officialTitle: Microsoft 365 settings enabled by default for newly created Engage communities
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states the rollout completes by mid-October 2026 and sets no action date; existing communities follow later this autumn with timing to be announced.
items.fingerprint: Newly created Viva Engage communities will have the Microsoft 365 group settings for member calendar and email subscriptions enabled by default, so members receive community emails and calendar invitations without opting in. Community owners can change it in the My Account portal. Rollout completes by mid-October 2026; existing communities follow later this autumn. Microsoft states no admin action is required.
items.why: A default that pushes community posts into every member's mailbox and calendar turns an Engage community into a distribution list nobody asked to join, and it is the community owner, not an administrator, who holds the switch. Where a community carries regulated or restricted discussion, its content now reaches mailboxes that are backed up, journalled and discoverable on different terms than the community itself.
items.action: Tell community owners the default has flipped and point them at the group settings in the My Account portal. Where a community exists precisely so its traffic stays out of mailboxes, have its owner turn the subscriptions off at creation, and check the retention and eDiscovery treatment of the group mailbox that now receives the copies.

items.title: Entra sign-in pages start enforcing a Content Security Policy in mid-October; injected scripts stop running on login.microsoftonline.com
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra ID: Enhance protection of the authentication experience by blocking external script injection
items.fingerprint: A Content Security Policy header is added to Entra ID browser sign-in pages on login.microsoftonline.com: scripts load only from trusted Microsoft CDN domains, inline scripts are restricted to Microsoft-authorised nonces, and extensions or tools that inject scripts may stop working; users can still sign in. MSAL/API flows and External ID custom domains are unaffected. GA worldwide mid-October to late October 2026; reminder of MC1191924.
items.why: Anything your organisation injects into the sign-in page — a password-manager or DLP browser extension, a session-recording or monitoring tool, a branding hack — stops running silently. The same header also blocks a malicious extension from scraping credentials there, which is the point.
items.action: Before 19 October, walk a sign-in on login.microsoftonline.com with the browser dev console open on a standard managed build and look for CSP violations in red; list every extension or tool that shows up and ask its vendor for a CSP-compliant version. Tell the help desk that a monitoring or SSO helper extension failing on the sign-in page after mid-October is expected.

items.title: Alert tuning rules can be scoped to specific detection sources; existing rules keep applying to every source, custom detections included
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender XDR: Detection source support in alert tuning rules
items.fingerprint: Alert tuning rules in Defender XDR gain detection source selection and apply only to the selected sources; rules not updated keep applying to all detection sources under their selected service sources, including custom detections. Public preview from mid-October 2026, GA from mid-November 2026.
items.why: An alert tuning rule is a suppression rule. Today a rule written for one noisy Defender for Endpoint detection also suppresses a custom detection that happens to match the same conditions, and nobody sees the alert it hid.
items.action: Export the current alert tuning rules and, for each one, note which detection source it was written for. When the setting arrives in mid-October, scope every rule to that source, starting with any rule broad enough to match your custom detections.

The investigation used Azure DevOps audit logs and Git history.

items.title: Conditional Access docs turn the unverified device-platform note into a warning and tell admins to pair the condition with compliance to stop user-agent spoofing
items.officialTitle: Conditional Access: Conditions
items.fingerprint: On 28 September 2026 Microsoft turned the existing Device platforms paragraph of Conditional Access: Conditions (platform read from user agent strings, which can be modified, so the information is not verified) into a WARNING box and added one sentence: use Conditional Access policies with this condition together with another policy, such as one requiring device compliance or app protection, to mitigate the risk of user agent spoofing.
items.fingerprintBefore: Plain paragraph: the device platform comes from information the device provides, such as user agent strings, which can be modified, so it is not verified; use it with Intune compliance or as part of a block statement.
items.why: The caveat is a year old, but Microsoft has now made it a warning and named the attack: user agent spoofing. A policy that grants or exempts on device platform alone can be satisfied by an attacker who changes a user agent string.
items.action: List Conditional Access policies whose only distinguishing condition is Device platforms and whose grant is not Block; pair each with device compliance or app protection, or turn it into a block statement.
items.sourceCommit: MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs b86e263a1b, 28 September 2026: Enhance device platform section with security note (#2112)
items.tier0Note: Conditional Access is the gate in front of every privileged sign-in; a condition that can be spoofed is a bypass if it is the only condition.

items.title: Phishing installs MSP360 RMM, which then drops ScreenConnect as a second remote-access channel
items.officialTitle: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft Security Blog
items.fingerprint: Microsoft observed phishing lures (meeting requests, Zoom and Google Meet installers, PDF reader updates, e-cards, DHL notices) delivering masqueraded MSP360 RMM 2.5.0.67 installers; MSP360 persists as Windows services and uses PowerShell to install ConnectWise ScreenConnect silently, which then deploys credential-access and collection tools. Defender detections named include SupportScam:Win32/RogueMSP.MU!MTB, 'Suspicious usage of remote management software' and 'Uncommon remote access software'.
items.why: Two signed, legitimate remote-management products stacked on one host give the actor redundant access that survives removal of either one, and most allow-lists treat both as normal IT tooling.
items.action: Hunt DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceNetworkEvents for MSP360 and ScreenConnect on hosts where neither is an approved tool, and enforce an application-control allow-list for RMM software; reset credentials on any host where an unapproved RMM instance is found.

items.title: Zimbra mail servers are being exploited through an unauthenticated SNMP-path command injection (CVE-2026-73570); Microsoft names eight Defender detections
items.officialTitle: Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft Security Blog only
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Threat Intelligence tracks exploitation of CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra Collaboration Suite before 10.1.20: an OS command injection in the SNMP notification path, reachable by a crafted SMTP request when zimbra-snmp is installed and SNMP notifications are on. Patch 20 July 2026, probing 28 July to 7 August, disclosure 13 August, then JSP webshells, reverse shells, privilege escalation and exfiltration. Detections named include Exploit:Linux/SnmpTrapCmdInject.A and Exploit:Linux/SnmpTrapJspDrop.A; hunting uses DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceFileEvents.
items.why: An internet-facing mail server that is not Exchange is often outside the SOC's usual coverage; this is post-disclosure mass exploitation with credential dumping of the Zimbra configuration.
items.action: Inventory Zimbra hosts (Defender Vulnerability Management software inventory), confirm 10.1.20 or later, remove zimbra-snmp or disable SNMP notifications, rotate Zimbra secrets and hunt DeviceProcessEvents for shells spawned by the Zimbra service account.

items.title: Windows settings backup turns on by default on 26H2 devices where the policy is Not Configured
items.officialTitle: Windows settings backup is now enabled by default for eligible devices
items.fingerprint: With Windows 11 version 26H2 (GA 29 September 2026) the Windows settings backup policy is enabled by default on devices where it is Not Configured, outside privacy-sensitive regions and sovereign clouds; explicit enable or disable is honoured, restore stays off unless configured, and users can still turn backup off.
items.why: User settings and the Store app list start leaving the device for Microsoft's cloud by default on every unconfigured 26H2 machine — a data-flow change that happens because nobody set a policy.
items.action: Decide the policy explicitly in Intune or Group Policy for 26H2 devices; if backup is not wanted, set it to disabled before the 26H2 rollout rings reach users. Confirm in your own tenant.

items.title: Work IQ business skills switch on by default: Copilot Chat and agents can read Dataverse data in new production environments from 30 September
items.officialTitle: Business Skills in Work IQ - Default On
items.fingerprint: From 30 September 2026 Business Applications in Work IQ — Dataverse search and query, semantic models, Business Skills and Dataverse in declarative agents — is on by default for NEW production environments with Microsoft Copilot Premium plus Power Apps Premium or Dynamics 365. Not enabled: environments created before that date, EU/EEA, non-production, government and FedRAMP. Admins can disable it.
items.why: Every new production environment from today exposes its model-driven app data to Copilot Chat and agents unless an admin turns it off.
items.action: Add a check to your environment-creation process: disable Business Applications in Work IQ where the data is not meant for Copilot, or confirm the Dataverse security roles already limit what agents can read. Confirm in your own tenant.

items.title: Two new Advanced Hunting tables, SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults, put user and admin email submissions into KQL in early October
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: New email submissions data in Advanced Hunting
items.fingerprint: Defender for Office 365 adds two Advanced Hunting tables, SubmissionEvents (email submission events) and SubmissionResults (the results of those submissions), usable in custom detections; public preview and GA both roll out worldwide in early October 2026. Microsoft states the table documentation ships with the release, so no column list is published yet.
items.why: User-reported phish and admin submissions become queryable beside EmailEvents and can drive custom detections — the reported-phish loop stops living only in the Submissions portal.
items.action: When the tables appear, build a detection that joins user-reported submissions to EmailEvents and alerts on reported mail that was delivered; do not write queries against the columns until Microsoft publishes the schema.

items.title: Exchange Online PowerShell enforces stricter sign-in from 31 March 2027; ExchangeOnlineManagement below 3.10.1 can fail to authenticate
items.officialTitle: Action Required: Upgrade ExchangeOnlineManagement PowerShell Module to Version 3.10.1 or Later
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states enforcement of strict logon requirements begins 31 March 2027 (rollout late March to late April 2027); the post's actionRequiredBy is 26 March 2027.
items.fingerprint: Security enhancements to Exchange Online PowerShell authentication shipped in ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.1; from 31 March 2027 earlier versions may fail interactive authentication, particularly PowerShell 7 with Web Account Manager disabled. Certificate-based auth, WAM-based auth and Windows PowerShell 5.x may be unaffected.
items.why: SOC and IR automation that connects to Exchange Online interactively from PowerShell 7 (mailbox audit pulls, inbox-rule sweeps, message trace) can stop authenticating on enforcement day.
items.action: Run Get-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -ListAvailable on every jump host and automation runner, upgrade to 3.10.1 or later, and re-test IR scripts that use interactive sign-in under PowerShell 7.

items.title: Microsoft plugin registry brings agents, skills, connectors and MCP servers under one admin catalog; users get a Plugins button by late November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Copilot: Introducing the Microsoft plugin registry for Microsoft Copilot experiences
items.fingerprint: A shared catalog to discover, publish and govern plugins — packages that bundle agents, skills, connectors and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — across Copilot Chat, Cowork, Code, Autopilot, Word, PowerPoint, Excel and SharePoint, managed under Tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Agent 365. Registry rollout late September to late October 2026; the Agents, Agents & Skills and Customize buttons become Plugins from late October to late November 2026.
items.why: An MCP server reaches tenant data with the user's token; a central registry is where you decide which ones users can acquire, so it is a data-access control and not only a UI rename.
items.action: Review which plugin capabilities (MCP servers and connectors above all) users may acquire under Tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and align it with your app-consent policy before the Plugins button reaches users.

items.title: Hybrid tenants with on-premises mailboxes and online archives, and tenants sharing free/busy with on-premises orgs, must keep EWS on
items.officialTitle: Impact of Exchange Online EWS Deprecation on Hybrid Rich Coexistence and Cross-org Sharing
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Exchange Team Blog only
items.fingerprint: Exchange Online EWS changes run between October 2026 and April 2027. Two on-premises scenarios still need EWS: hybrid with on-premises mailboxes that have Exchange Online archives (Graph-based rich coexistence does not fully support it yet) and an on-premises org with an organization relationship to another Exchange Online tenant. Microsoft says keep the tenant's EWSEnabled TRUE and add the dedicated Exchange hybrid application to EWSAllowedAppIDs.
items.why: The EWS shutdown that starts today is also an attack-surface reduction; this post is Microsoft telling some tenants to keep EWS enabled, so the exception must be scoped to one app ID rather than left open.
items.action: If you have on-premises mailboxes with online archives or org relationships with on-premises partners, confirm EWSEnabled is TRUE and that EWSAllowedAppIDs lists only the dedicated hybrid app; do not remove the on-premises servers' EWS permissions yet.

items.title: Defender unified RBAC custom roles can now be assigned to GDAP partner groups, scoped per product and data source (preview)
items.officialTitle: What’s new in Microsoft Sentinel: September 2026
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft Sentinel Blog only
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's September Sentinel roundup: Case Management in Defender (public preview from 23 September 2026), unified RBAC custom roles assignable to GDAP remote tenant groups and scoped to specific security products, data sources and data collections (public preview; GDAP previously supported only Entra directory roles), multi-account support for Codeless Connector Framework connectors (preview), and more than 500 data connectors.
items.why: MSSP access can now be cut down from an Entra directory role to a scoped Defender role — and the partner, not you, controls who sits in the GDAP group that receives it.
items.action: For each MSSP relationship, replace broad Entra roles delegated through GDAP with a scoped unified RBAC custom role, and review which partner groups hold it.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states three dates for Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True and no list: 2 October 2026 the affected tenants are identified, 8-9 October Microsoft populates EWSAllowedAppIDs from 60 days of observed EWS activity, 10 October the list becomes required.
items.title: EWS needs an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list from 10 October; EWSEnabled=True alone stops being enough
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Exchange Online: Exchange Web Services (EWS) enforcement update for EWSAllowedAppIDs
items.fingerprint: From 10 October 2026 a Worldwide tenant with EWSEnabled=True must also carry an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list; an application that is not on it may lose EWS access. Microsoft identifies affected tenants on 2 October and on 8-9 October creates the list from the previous 60 days of EWS activity, so infrequently used applications may be missed. The list is a replacement list, changes take up to 24 hours, tenants with EWSEnabled unset are switched off by the phased retirement, and a tenant with a configured list keeps its setting until April 2027. Rollout runs to early July 2027.
items.why: The list Microsoft generates is built from 60 days of traffic, so the quarterly job, the archive tool and the IR script that reads mailboxes over EWS are exactly what it misses. After 10 October the allow list is also the complete inventory of applications that can still reach mailboxes over EWS, which makes it a control worth owning rather than inheriting.
items.action: Before 10 October run Get-OrganizationConfig -RetrieveEwsOperationAccessPolicy | Format-List EwsAllowedAppIDs, compare it with the EWS usage report, add every AppID the business still needs in one write (the list is replaced, not appended), and record who approved each entry.

items.tier0Note: Retires an authentication method for external users and replaces it with Entra B2B guest accounts, which fall under Conditional Access and guest lifecycle policy.
items.deadlineNote: (inferred) Microsoft's 1 October 2026 update says Phase 2 begins in mid-October 2026 and completes by end of November 2026 for Production environments; 15 October 2026 is this brief's reading of "mid-October". GCC, GCC High and DoD are excluded and undated.
items.title: SharePoint one-time passcode retirement slips: Phase 2 now starts mid-October and runs to the end of November
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Retirement of SharePoint One-Time Passcode (SPO OTP) and transition to Microsoft Entra B2B
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised MC1243549 on 1 October 2026: retirement of SharePoint and OneDrive one-time passcode authentication (Phase 2) begins in mid-October 2026 and completes by end of November 2026 for Production environments, instead of 1 to 31 October. Once it reaches a tenant, an external user without an Entra B2B guest account is denied on previously shared specific-people links until a guest account exists or the content is re-shared. GCC, GCC High and DoD remain excluded.
items.fingerprintBefore: Phase 2, the retirement of SharePoint Online OTP, rescheduled to begin on 1 October and expected to complete by 31 October for Production environments (update of 17 July 2026).
items.why: Every external recipient who still signs in with an emailed code becomes an Entra B2B guest or loses access. That moves external sharing under Conditional Access and guest governance, and it produces a wave of new guest objects and of access-denied tickets on old links, both of which look like incidents if nobody expects them.
items.action: Use the extra two weeks: confirm the Conditional Access policies that target guests behave as intended for SharePoint and OneDrive, check the cross-tenant access and B2B collaboration settings that the automatic invitations will use, and brief the service desk on access denied for old specific-people links.

items.tier0Note: Touches a tier-0 control: Conditional Access, an authentication method, a privileged role or an app consent path.
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft's roadmap entry states the release phase, General Availability, and no date.
items.title: Passkeys for B2B guests: a resource tenant will issue its own passkeys to guest users, on by default
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra ID: Passkey support for B2B users
items.fingerprint: Roadmap 569432, created 1 October 2026, status In development, release phase General Availability: B2B users, internal guests and external users alike, will register and sign in with passkeys issued by the resource tenant to meet that tenant's MFA requirement, from My Security Info, an in-line proof-up prompt or a passkey registration campaign. The change is on by default; B2B users already in scope for passkeys in the Authentication methods policy are enabled automatically.
items.why: A guest will hold a phishing-resistant credential that lives in your tenant rather than in theirs. That closes the gap in which guests satisfied MFA only through their home tenant, and it also means guest accounts start carrying authentication methods your tenant must govern, audit and revoke.
items.action: Review who the passkey (FIDO2) policy in Authentication methods targets today: if it targets All users, guests are in scope the day this ships. Decide whether guests should register resource-tenant passkeys, then adjust the target groups, the registration campaign and the Conditional Access policies before rollout.

items.tier0Note: A hidden application permission whose name refers to blocking Connect Sync sits on the write path of hybrid identity synchronisation.
items.title: The deployment map gains MS-ConnectSyncBlocked.ReadWrite.All on the legacy Azure AD Graph resource and two hidden PrintBadges scopes
items.officialTitle: Weekly Permissions sync 2026-10-01 (#1646)
items.fingerprint: provisioningInfo.json went from 1,943 to 1,946 names in Microsoft's permissions sync of 1 October 2026 (commit b9a67f1, 14:00 UTC). Three names are new and none left: MS-ConnectSyncBlocked.ReadWrite.All, Application, hidden and enabled, on resource 00000002-0000-0000-c000-000000000000; PrintBadges.Read.All and PrintBadges.ReadWrite.All, DelegatedWork, hidden, enabled, public ring, on resource da9b70f6-5323-4ce6-ae5c-88dcc5082966. None of the three is in permissions.json or in the Graph service principal this brief reads, and the deployment record carries no GUID.
items.why: MS-ConnectSyncBlocked.ReadWrite.All is an application permission, hidden and already enabled, on the legacy directory resource rather than on Microsoft Graph. Microsoft publishes no description, so what it blocks is not stated; the name places it on the Entra Connect Sync path, and a write permission there is a tier-0 capability the day it becomes grantable.
items.action: Nothing is grantable from this alone: the names are hidden and not in this tenant's service principal. Add MS-ConnectSyncBlocked.ReadWrite.All to the watch list for app role assignments on the Windows Azure Active Directory resource, and treat its first appearance in a tenant as a consent event to review.

items.title: Defender Antivirus platform 4.18.26080.4 is documented: it fixes the false "Microsoft Defender Antivirus is turned off" notification
items.officialTitle: Windows Antivirus | August 2026-2 | Platform 4.18.26080.4 | Engine 1.1.26080.3
items.publishedNote: 17 September 2026 is the date Microsoft prints for the platform build; the release-notes page gained the section in the documentation mirror's 1 October 2026 read, which is why the row is dated inside the period by its revision.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's Defender for Endpoint release notes gained the section Windows Antivirus, August 2026-2: platform 4.18.26080.4 dated 17 September 2026, engine 1.1.26080.3 and security intelligence 1.159.11.0 dated 1 September 2026, support phase Security and Critical Updates. The one listed change fixes Windows incorrectly showing that Microsoft Defender Antivirus is turned off at start-up or intermittently afterwards while it stayed active. The same page edit added Linux rows: libcurl upgraded to 8.20.0 for CVE-2026-7168, scheduled antivirus scans generally available, and vulnerability detection for Node.js, Python and Java libraries.
items.why: A notification that antivirus is off, on a device where it is on, generates tickets and teaches users to ignore the real warning. The platform build is also the support line: two builds back drops to technical upgrade support only.
items.action: Check the AMProductVersion spread in the Defender portal device health report or in DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessment; devices still below 4.18.26080.4 after the gradual rollout are the ones whose update ring is stuck.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states public preview is available now and general availability begins mid-November 2026, completing late December 2026; no action date.
items.title: Entra App Gallery gets self-service onboarding for publishers: preview now, general availability from mid-November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra App Gallery: Self-service onboarding for new applications
items.fingerprint: Independent software vendors can validate OIDC, SAML and provisioning integrations, submit a new application to the Microsoft Entra App Gallery and track the review from the Entra admin center. Public preview now; general availability worldwide from mid-November to late December 2026. Existing gallery applications keep the current update and removal process, and nothing changes in how users access applications.
items.why: Gallery listing is the signal many tenants use to decide an application is safe to consent to. A faster publishing path means more gallery applications; it does not change what a gallery listing verifies.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states the add-ons retire beginning 1 November 2026; the post's action-required date is 1 November 2026.
items.title: AI Builder capacity add-ons retire on 1 November; existing credits last to the end of the subscription term
items.officialTitle: Microsoft AI Builder: Retirement of AI Builder capacity add-ons
items.fingerprint: AI Builder capacity add-ons retire beginning 1 November 2026: they can no longer be renewed or purchased, existing credits stay usable to the end of the current term, and continued AI Builder use moves to Copilot Credits. Microsoft asks organisations with active add-ons to turn off recurring billing before the next renewal.
items.why: A licensing change with no security content; it is here because it carries a date inside 60 days and an administrator action.
items.action: Hand to whoever owns Power Platform licensing: turn off recurring billing on AI Builder capacity add-ons before the next renewal and plan Copilot Credits.

items.tier0Note: On-premises Exchange servers hold write rights over AD DS objects through the Exchange Trusted Subsystem group, so an Exchange host one update behind is a tier-0-adjacent asset. The CVE itself grants mailbox read, not directory write; the tier-0 flag is this brief's classification of the host (inferred), the same one the 24 September Exchange update carries.
items.title: Exchange Server gets a V2 of the September security updates: CVE-2026-96940 lets a signed-in user read other people's mailboxes
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Exchange Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
items.fingerprint: MSRC published CVE-2026-96940 on 2 October 2026, outside the monthly cadence: weak authorization in Exchange Server lets an authenticated attacker gain access to other users' mailboxes in the same organization and read messages and attachments. Important, CVSS 8.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N), Exploited: No, Publicly disclosed: No, Exploitation More Likely. Fixed builds: Exchange SE RTM 15.02.2562.053 (KB5129955), 2019 CU15 15.02.1748.053 (KB5129956), 2019 CU14 15.02.1544.048 (KB5129957), 2016 CU23 15.01.2507.075 (KB5129958); the 2016 and 2019 updates are available only under the Period 2 ESU program. Exchange Online already carries a service-side fix. The Exchange Team blog says the only difference between the 24 September release and V2 is this CVE.
items.why: A server patched with the 24 September set is not patched for this. Any valid low-privilege mailbox account is enough to read another mailbox, Microsoft rates exploitation as more likely, and a server that reports the September update as installed will look compliant unless the build number is checked.
items.action: Run the Exchange Health Checker and confirm every Exchange SE, 2019 and 2016 server is on the 2 October build (SE RTM 15.02.2562.053 or the matching 2019/2016 ESU build), not the 24 September one; treat a server still on the earlier build as unpatched.

items.deadlineNote: (inferred) Microsoft writes: “Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.” It prints no calendar day; 1 November 2026 is this brief's reading of “early November”.
items.title: Security Operator loses default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List under Defender Unified RBAC, from early November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Changes to Unified RBAC permission mapping for Microsoft Entra Security Operator role
items.fingerprint: From early November 2026 the default Unified RBAC mapping of the Entra Security Operator role for Defender for Office 365 no longer includes Authorization and settings\Security settings (All permissions). Where Unified RBAC is enabled for Email & Collaboration, Security Operator alone will no longer view, create, edit or delete anti-spam, anti-phishing, anti-malware, Safe Links, Safe Attachments or preset security policies, nor view or change Tenant Allow/Block List entries. Tenants without Unified RBAC are not affected, and other role mappings and Exchange Online PowerShell authorization are unchanged. Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD; complete by early December 2026.
items.why: Adding a block entry to the Tenant Allow/Block List is a routine containment step in a phishing incident. An analyst who holds only Security Operator will find that step denied mid-incident some day in November, with no error that names this change.
items.action: List who holds Entra Security Operator and uses it for email threat policies or the Tenant Allow/Block List; before November assign those people the Unified RBAC permissions Core security settings and Detection tuning, or a role that includes them, and test a block entry with a Security Operator-only account.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft writes that devices “may lose calendar functionality starting October 2026” and that rollout runs from early October 2026 to late April 2027; it prints no calendar day, so no deadline date is carried.
items.title: Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones and panels below the February 2026 app version lose their calendar as EWS is switched off from October
items.officialTitle: Action required: Update Teams devices to a minimum app version ahead of the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS)
items.fingerprint: Two identical posts of 2 October 2026 (MC1486288 tagged Teams, MC1486282 tagged Microsoft 365 and Teams): Teams devices used EWS for calendar and moved to a replacement in February 2026. Devices below the minimum app version may lose calendar sync as EWS is disabled from October 2026: Teams Rooms on Android 1449/1.0.96.2025421910, Teams phones 1449/1.0.94.2025460012, Teams panels 1449/1.0.97.2025385601. Rooms lose one-touch join, phones lose the meeting list, panels stop showing availability and booking; calling is not affected.
items.why: This is the same EWS switch-off as the 10 October EWSAllowedAppIDs enforcement, seen from the meeting room. A room that cannot join its own meeting is reported as a Teams outage, and the cause is a firmware ring nobody was watching.
items.action: In the Teams admin center or the Pro Management portal, filter Teams devices by app version, update everything below the three minimums, and check for devices that are offline or excluded from update rings.

items.title: The September 2026 Scan Cab was re-issued on 2 October to carry the new Exchange Server update; a copy downloaded earlier does not detect it
items.officialTitle: An updated version of the September 2026 Scan Cab is available
items.fingerprint: Microsoft re-published wsusscn2.cab at 6:30 PM PDT on 2 October 2026 with metadata for the Exchange Server update that addresses CVE-2026-96940 (KB5129955 for Exchange SE). Administrators who downloaded the September Scan Cab before that time and use it to assess Exchange Server should re-acquire and re-deploy it. Microsoft notes that non-Microsoft tools may also consume the Scan Cab. The post is flagged a major change.
items.why: An offline compliance scan fed by the older cab reports an Exchange server as fully patched while it is missing the 2 October fix. That is a false negative in exactly the report used to prove the server is safe.
items.action: If any scanner or script in the estate reads wsusscn2.cab, download it again and re-run the scan against Exchange servers; check with the vendor whether third-party patch tools refresh it automatically.

items.title: Endpoint Privilege Management gains a third policy type: standard users can change IPv4, IPv6 and DNS settings without administrator rights
items.officialTitle: Manage system settings with Endpoint Privilege Management
items.fingerprint: A new Learn page published 2 October 2026 documents the elevation system settings policy for Endpoint Privilege Management on Windows. A rule with System setting = Network settings and Elevation type = User confirmed lets a standard user change IPv4, IPv6 and DNS server values for the device's adapters from the Windows Company Portal (Help & support > System settings), even offline. Validation is optional: a business justification, Windows authentication, both or neither. The EPM overview now names three policy types instead of two.
items.why: DNS is a security control on most estates: protective DNS, the proxy auto-configuration path and Global Secure Access all assume the resolver is the managed one. A rule with no validation lets a user, or malware in the user's session that can drive the Company Portal flow, point a device at a resolver of its choosing.
items.action: If EPM is licensed, decide who may hold this policy before someone creates it; require both business justification and Windows authentication on every rule, scope it to the travelling users who need it, and review the justifications in EPM reporting.

items.title: Android corporate-owned work profile: Microsoft corrects the factory reset protection table, and a Settings reset is unprotected when FRP emails are not configured
items.officialTitle: Android Enterprise device restriction settings in Microsoft Intune
items.fingerprint: Two Intune pages were republished on 2 October 2026. In the Android Enterprise device restrictions reference the COPE row of the factory reset protection table changed its first cell from no factory reset protection to factory reset protection, and a sentence was added: for COPE devices, a Settings reset doesn't enforce FRP when Factory reset protection emails is Not configured. The corporate enrollment methods page carries the same sentence and now limits the Android 15 re-entry requirement to devices where FRP emails are configured.
items.why: A lost or stolen corporate-owned work profile device with no FRP email configured can be wiped from Settings and set up again by whoever holds it. The earlier table did not say that.
items.action: Check the device restriction profiles assigned to COPE devices and set Factory reset protection emails wherever it reads Not configured.

items.title: The Data Security AI Admin role is now described as editing Data Loss Prevention policies in general, no longer only those related to Copilot
items.officialTitle: Roles and role groups in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 and Microsoft Purview
items.fingerprint: Microsoft republished the role-group reference on 2 October 2026 (17:37 UTC). In both the Data Security AI Admins role group row and the Data Security AI Admin role row, the words related to Copilot were removed: the role is now for editing Data Loss Prevention policies and viewing AI content in Data Security Posture Management. Nothing else on the page changed. Whether the service-side permission widened or the description was corrected is not stated by Microsoft.
items.why: If the description now matches what the role can do, everyone already in Data Security AI Admins can edit every DLP policy, not only the Copilot ones. A role assigned as a narrow AI-governance role would then be a DLP administrator.
items.action: List the members of the Data Security AI Admins role group and check in the Purview portal whether they can edit a non-Copilot DLP policy; remove anyone who should not be able to.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft writes: public preview rolls out from early October to mid October 2026 and general availability from mid November to late November 2026; no action date is stated.
items.title: Purview brings sensitive information types, Exact Data Match, trainable classifiers and fingerprinting into one Classifiers experience: preview this month, GA in November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview |Unified Classification Management Experience
