items.title: Dataverse records can be secured by the value of a column instead of by record ownership (public preview)
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration - Secure Dataverse record with column-based filtering
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 2 October 2026: admins can use filtered views to grant record-level access in Dataverse based on the value of a field, such as region or department, rather than on record ownership. Public preview from 2 October 2026; Microsoft states no action is required.
items.why: A second access model beside ownership and sharing. Access reviews that reason from record ownership will not see grants made this way.
items.action: No action required; if makers adopt it, include filtered-view security in the next Dataverse access review.

items.title: Private Access Sensor 2.2.79 for domain controllers: updates now install themselves, the local registry break-glass override is gone, and Kerberos enforcement extends to UDP
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra Private Access Sensor release history — Version 2.2.79
items.tier0Note: The sensor is installed on domain controllers and enforces Kerberos policy there; from 2.2.79 future sensor builds download and install themselves on that host. Tier-0 classification of the host is this brief's (inferred).
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's release history page gained a Version 2.2.79 section on 5 October 2026 (entra-docs commit 3977e05ee); Microsoft dates the release itself 29 September 2026. The release adds automatic download and installation of future sensor updates; upgrading from 2.2.42 needs a one-time install of the full installer from the Entra admin center to enable over-the-air updates. Security enhancements: Kerberos policy enforcement extends to UDP alongside TCP, network packet validation is hardened and the local registry break-glass override is removed in favor of cloud policy. Non-wildcard SPNs and requested Kerberos service names are now matched by the owning Active Directory account SID, which extends protection to aliases of the same account. Upgrade considerations: allow inbound TCP and UDP on port 1337; IPv6 Kerberos traffic is unsupported and blocked.
items.why: The Private Access Sensor runs on domain controllers and decides which Kerberos requests are allowed, so three things change on a tier-0 host at once: the sensor now updates itself from the cloud, the on-box registry override an administrator could use to bypass enforcement in an outage no longer exists, and Kerberos over UDP is enforced where only TCP was. A site that relied on the registry break-glass has lost its local way out, and an IPv6-only Kerberos path stops working.
items.action: List the domain controllers that run the Private Access Sensor and their versions; before upgrading from 2.2.42 open inbound TCP and UDP 1337, confirm no client depends on Kerberos over IPv6, replace any runbook step that uses the registry break-glass with the cloud policy equivalent, and decide who approves self-installing updates on domain controllers.

items.title: Final reminder: the MemberOf rule operator stops processing on 3 November, and dynamic groups built on it freeze in their last state

Organizations using it in dynamic groups, administrative units or entitlement policies must replace those configurations before the deadline. After retirement, 'Dynamic groups using MemberOf will stop processing membership changes' and 'existing membership and assignment data will remain in their last known state.' items.title: Twelve Graph permissions became grantable: write access to provisioning-job synchronization metadata, Sentinel Content Hub packages and tenant-defined custom objects

The twelve new application roles are SynchronizationMetadata.Read.All, .Read.OwnedBy, .ReadWrite.All and .ReadWrite.OwnedBy; ContentHub-Catalog.Read.All, ContentHub-Installed.Read.All and ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All; CustomObject.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All; CustomObjectDefinition.Read.All, .ReadBasic.All and .ReadWrite.All. Ten of them also arrive as delegated scopes requiring admin consent; the two OwnedBy roles are application only. All are enabled, none is in the permissions reference, and all twelve had been in Microsoft's deployment map since September or earlier. Afternoon pass, 6 October: the next dump of the same service principal (merill/microsoft-info 531674a, 12:09 UTC) does not carry the twelve names and is byte-identical to the dumps of 29 September and 1 October, 748 application roles and 828 delegated scopes. One read holds them and the next does not, so treat them as rolling out and not as settled; the catalog entries are left as the morning wrote them until a third read decides. Read again on 7 October: the dump of 6 October 12:09 UTC (531674a) had gone back to 748 application roles and 828 delegated scopes without the twelve, and the next one, 6 October 21:48 UTC (9c21ffa), carries 760 and 838 again with all twelve names. ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All can 'create, update, and delete installed packages and package-scoped content items', which is the installed security content of the organization. CustomObjectDefinition.ReadWrite.All manages a directory data surface Microsoft has not documented.

items.title: Entra Kerberos gets one configuration guide: the key-rotation page is folded into it, with a stated rotation practice and a warning that only Set-AzureADKerberosServer may rotate the key
items.officialTitle: Configure Microsoft Entra Kerberos trust
items.tier0Note: The Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object lives in on-premises Active Directory and its key protects the ticket-granting tickets Entra ID issues; the page describes it as functioning like a read-only domain controller.
items.fingerprint: Commit 1c41e71 of 8 October 2026 adds 'Configure Microsoft Entra Kerberos trust' (305 lines, ms.date 10/07/2026), removes 'Rotate the Kerberos server key' and redirects it to the new page. The new page covers creating the Trusted Domain Object, client configuration, key rotation, and removing the object. On rotation: 'Microsoft doesn't mandate a fixed rotation interval. Rotate the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server key on the same schedule as other Active Directory Kerberos (krbtgt) keys, during scheduled security maintenance windows, and immediately after a suspected credential compromise.' And: 'Other tools can rotate krbtgt keys, but you must use the Set-AzureADKerberosServer cmdlet for the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server.'
items.why: Tenants that use cloud Kerberos trust for Windows Hello for Business or FIDO2 sign-in to on-premises resources carry a second krbtgt-class key that many krbtgt rotation runbooks do not touch. Microsoft now says in one place that it belongs on the same schedule and in the same incident-response step.
items.action: Check whether the krbtgt rotation runbook and the compromise-recovery plan name the Entra Kerberos server key; if not, add Set-AzureADKerberosServer -RotateServerKey to both, and update bookmarks to the new page.

items.title: Conditional Access baseline-scope enforcement: the page now speaks of the rollout in the past tense and adds a Graph query that lists the policies it affects
items.officialTitle: Conditional Access enforcement for resource exclusions (baseline scopes)
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Commit 3c73d53 of 8 October 2026, 'Revise enforcement model details and rollout date': 'Rollout of the enforcement model for baseline scopes began on June 15, 2026' where the page read 'begins'; 'If you haven't made any changes to the baseline scopes settings, the enforcement is enabled automatically', with the words 'over a period of approximately several weeks' removed. Added: a Graph query, conditionalAccess/policies filtered on includeApplications 'All' with any excludeApplications, that lists the All-resources policies with at least one resource exclusion; and the sign-in log example now spans 15 June to 15 July 2026. No new date is stated.
items.why: Sign-ins that request only baseline scopes used to pass an All-resources policy that carried exclusions; with enforcement they must satisfy it. The page no longer describes that as upcoming, so an unexplained Conditional Access prompt or failure on such an application is now expected behaviour rather than a fault.
items.action: Run the Graph query Microsoft added to list the policies in scope, and filter sign-in logs on the placeholder audience to see which applications are affected in your tenant.

items.title: RD Web Access stops rendering when browsers switch off XSLT; Microsoft publishes KB5130994 with workarounds
items.officialTitle: Take action to prevent RD Web Access rendering failures
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Message Center, 8 October 2026, marked a major change: 'The Remote Desktop Web Access (RD Web Access) experience included with Windows Server relies on Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations (XSLT) to render its web interface. Chromium-based and other browsers are disabling XSLT support in the short term.' After that, users 'might encounter a page that fails to render as expected' and 'might be unable to access remote resources'. Microsoft points to KB5130994, 'RD Web Access fails to load when XSLT is disabled in Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome'. No date is stated.
items.why: For organisations that still publish RemoteApp or desktops through RD Web Access this is an outage driven by a browser update, not by a Windows patch, so it will not line up with a change window. Expect the workaround that reaches users first to be an older or unmanaged browser.
items.action: Find out whether RD Web Access is still in use, read KB5130994, and choose the workaround before the browser channel you manage disables XSLT.

items.title: Copilot starts using inferences from Microsoft 365 work data for personalised answers; one admin control, enhancedPersonalizationSetting, turns it off
items.officialTitle: Enhanced M365 Copilot Memory - Copilot is now personalized with work data
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Message Center, 8 October 2026: 'Copilot now uses inferences Microsoft 365 data as context to provide more personalized responses to your work.' General availability, Worldwide, from early to late October 2026. Users can switch off the 'Chat History and Work Insights' toggle under Settings > Personalization, and 'Admins can disable this setting with the enhancedPersonalizationSetting admin control'. Microsoft states no admin action is required and names no compliance consideration.
items.why: Inferences derived from mail, files and chats become a stored input to later answers. That is a data-handling change which arrives on by default, in the month it was announced, and with a single tenant control.
items.action: Decide with the data-protection owner whether work insights stay on, and set enhancedPersonalizationSetting before the rollout completes in late October if they do not.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft's own date: 'Beginning January 1, 2027'; rollout early to mid-January 2027.
items.title: Viva Glint survey mail will come from the tenant's default domain from 1 January 2027 unless a custom sending domain is configured
items.officialTitle: Viva Glint: Change to the default email sending domain
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Message Center, 8 October 2026: 'Beginning January 1, 2027, Viva Glint survey notification emails will use your organization's default domain if you have not configured a custom sending domain in the M365 admin center, instead of no-reply@glint.mail.microsoft. Your default domain may look like contoso.onmicrosoft.com.' Microsoft adds that 'Email filtering rules that reference the current sender may need to be updated' and asks that allow-list changes be scoped 'to your specific sending domain—not all of onmicrosoft.com'.
items.why: Survey mail with links, arriving from an onmicrosoft.com address, is what users are trained to report and what transport rules are written to quarantine. The safe fix is a verified custom domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, not a broad allow-list entry.
items.action: If Viva Glint is in use, configure the custom sending domain and validate SPF, DKIM and DMARC before January; refuse any request to allow-list onmicrosoft.com as a whole.

items.title: Zendesk connections in Microsoft API Hub move to expiring tokens: 48-hour access tokens, 90-day refresh tokens, and existing connections must be reauthorised
items.officialTitle: Microsoft API Hub: Zendesk OAuth tokens will require expiration and automatic refresh
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Message Center, 8 October 2026: new Zendesk connections and connections reauthorised after rollout 'will receive access tokens that expire after 48 hours, refresh tokens that expire after 90 days, and automatic token refresh support'. 'Existing Zendesk connections created before this change cannot be automatically migrated' and 'Flows that rely on existing Zendesk connections may fail until those connections are reauthorized.' Rollout early October 2026 to late January 2027.
items.why: A long-lived third-party token held by a connector is replaced by a short-lived one, which is a gain; the cost is that an automation feeding tickets from security tooling into Zendesk can stop without an alert.
items.action: If any SOC or service-desk flow uses the Zendesk connector, reauthorise its connection and add a failure notification to the flow.

items.title: Copilot URL redirect: the remaining users move to copilot.cloud.microsoft in early November, a month later than Microsoft last wrote
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Allow connections to copilot.cloud.microsoft before the Copilot URL redirect
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 27 August 2026, revised on 8 October 2026: 'Updated October 8, 2026: We have updated the content.' The rollout section now reads 'In early November, 2026 Microsoft will redirect the remaining users who had not been redirected in early September'; the 21 September version said early October. Unchanged: 'Backend services and Copilot in Edge will require connection to *.cloud.microsoft', the request to add *.cloud.microsoft to allow lists, and the note that tenants following the recommended network configuration need no change.
items.why: The control in question is an egress allow list. A proxy or secure web gateway that still blocks part of *.cloud.microsoft has four more weeks, and the failure when it comes looks like a Copilot outage rather than a blocked URL.
items.action: Run the Microsoft 365 Connectivity Test for *.cloud.microsoft from a managed network and fix proxy, firewall and tenant-restriction rules before November.

items.title: New Copilot Pages and Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive from mid-October, two months later than first announced; DLP, retention and eDiscovery for OneDrive then apply
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Pages and Notebooks Creation in OneDrive
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 6 August 2026, revised on 8 October 2026: 'Updated October 8, 2026: We have updated the timeline.' 'General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 (previously mid-August) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously late September)'; GCC, GCC High and DoD from mid-November to early December 2026. Newly created Copilot Pages and new Copilot Notebooks are stored in the user's OneDrive for Business; existing Pages stay where they are and existing Notebooks keep using SharePoint Embedded. OneDrive DLP policies, retention labels, Information Barriers and path-based eDiscovery apply to the new content.
items.why: AI-generated working documents move into a store the SOC and compliance teams already monitor, which closes a gap: until the change, Pages sat outside OneDrive DLP and outside the departed-user workflow. During the rollout the same tenant has Pages in two places.
items.action: Confirm that the OneDrive DLP and retention policies you rely on cover the new content, and tell investigators that Pages created before the change are not in OneDrive.

items.title: Windows 11 26H2 security baseline is reissued as v2: Administrator protection is now part of it, with credential prompts on the secure desktop
items.officialTitle: Windows 11, version 26H2 security baseline
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Baselines Blog, as it stood in the feed on 8 October 2026: 'The Windows 11, version 26H2 security baseline has been updated to reflect the general availability of Administrator protection. An updated v2 package is now available, and organizations should review and test the existing Administrator protection configuration as appropriate for their environment.' Marked updated in the change table: 'User Account Control: Configure type of Admin Approval Mode' is 'Admin Approval Mode with Administrator protection', and the elevation prompt for administrators is 'Prompt for credentials on the secure desktop'. Also in the baseline: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 in place of TLS 1.1 and 1.2 for the Internet Control Panel setting, and Windows Ready Print driver ranking enabled.
items.why: Administrator protection replaces the split-token admin session with a separate, just-in-time elevation that asks for credentials. A baseline that enables it changes how every local-admin elevation looks in the logs and breaks tools that relied on silent elevation.
items.action: Take the v2 package from the Security Compliance Toolkit, test Administrator protection on admin workstations first, and brief the help desk on the new credential prompt.

items.title: A Purview DLP policy can now keep Microsoft 365 Copilot from grounding answers in mail received from external senders
items.officialTitle: Protecting Organizations from External Email Risks in Microsoft 365 Copilot
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Community blog, 8 October 2026: 'A new policy in Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) addresses exactly this challenge. It lets organizations ground Copilot in trusted internal email only—reducing the risk of cross-prompt injection'. It is configured as 'a DLP policy configured in the Microsoft Purview portal using the "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat" policy location with the "Email is received from > External users" condition', and 'With this new policy enabled, the external email is excluded from grounding entirely'. The post states no licence requirement and no rollout date in the part this brief read.
items.why: Indirect prompt injection through an inbound message is the attack on Copilot that needs no access to the tenant at all. This is a tenant-side control for it that does not depend on detecting the injected text.
items.action: Pilot the policy on a group that receives a lot of external mail and measure what Copilot stops being able to answer before widening it.

items.title: Purview DLP can stop Copilot from using external web search for a prompt that contains sensitive information types
items.officialTitle: Why DLP for External Web Search in Microsoft 365 Copilot Matters?
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Community blog, 8 October 2026: the feature 'keeps sensitive information from reaching external web search during Copilot's query generation'. In Microsoft's summary, 'admin and user toggles decide whether Copilot can search the web; Microsoft Purview DLP decides what data may leave when it does', and it 'Prevents Copilot from using external web search as a grounding source for that prompt. It does not block the prompt itself'. The post also restates that generated queries, not whole prompts or files, go to the Bing search service with user and tenant identifiers removed.
items.why: Until now the web-search control for Copilot was on or off. A content-aware control means web grounding can stay enabled for ordinary work while a prompt carrying a card number or a passport number stays inside the tenant boundary.
items.action: Add the Copilot location to the DLP policy that already defines your sensitive information types, in audit mode first, and review matches for a week.

items.title: Sending from aliases is generally available in Exchange Online: a user can send as any proxy address on the mailbox once the tenant switch is on
items.officialTitle: Sending From Email Aliases – General Availability
items.tier0Note: No write path into AD DS, a domain controller, a sync or provisioning host, a certification authority, a Global-Administrator-equivalent role or federation.
items.fingerprint: Exchange Team Blog, 8 October 2026: 'Today we are announcing the General Availability (GA) of Sending from Aliases for Exchange Online.' It is enabled per tenant with Set-OrganizationConfig -SendFromAliasEnabled $True or in the Exchange admin center under Settings > Mail Flow; 'It might take up to 60 minutes for this change to take effect'. An administrator 'who wishes to block a domain from being able to send can set the domain as Receive Only in the M365 Admin Center'.
items.why: With the switch on, the From address of an internal sender is no longer always the primary SMTP address. Detections, transport rules and investigations that key on the primary address miss mail sent from an alias, and an old alias on a retired domain becomes a sending identity again.
items.action: Before enabling it, mark domains that should never send as Receive Only and check that sender-based rules and hunting queries resolve aliases to the mailbox.

graphMap.rule: resource = first path segment that is not a parameter; /me/... counts as users. Directory action microsoft.directory/<resource>[/<property>]/<operation>; a .unified or .security suffix on the resource falls back to its base. GET maps to read, POST to create, PATCH and PUT to update, DELETE to delete. A role covers an endpoint when it holds an action on the same resource with the same operation, or allTasks on that resource. Coverage is the share of the permission's ENDPOINTS, never the count of the role's actions. Depth is whole resource when the matching action carries allProperties or allTasks, and selected properties only otherwise.
graphMap.ruleNote: Derived by this brief, not published by Microsoft. Microsoft publishes no role-to-permission mapping: permissions.json carries authorizationType, ownerInfo, pathSets and schemes and no role field at all, and the 136 role source files in MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs name no Graph permission.

components.name: Entra Connect Sync
components.deadlineNote: Synchronization stops on any server below the version whose support ends on this date.

items.text: This release includes security fixes. We recommend upgrading to this version as soon as possible.
09/23/2026: Released for download via the Microsoft Entra admin center. This is a hotfix release.

Fixed an issue in version 2.6.91.0 where enabling Pass-through Authentication through the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard could fail while registering the locally installed Microsoft Entra Connect Authentication Agent.
This release includes security fixes. We recommend upgrading to this version as soon as possible.

Added a guided migration workflow from Microsoft Entra Connect Sync to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. The workflow includes configuration assessment, provisioning agent setup, staged activation, and validation. This feature is available only in the Azure public cloud.
Added support for an additional sovereign cloud environment, including Pass-through Authentication, Seamless Single Sign-On, password writeback, and Health Agent monitoring.

Phishing-resistant authentication in the Microsoft Entra Connect setup wizard is now generally available and enabled by default. The Windows Web Account Manager prompt supports passkeys, FIDO2 security keys, and passwords, reuses the signed-in session across Microsoft Entra services, and preserves Seamless Single Sign-On Kerberos key rotation.

Cloud configuration cmdlets no longer require an explicit -AADUserName. When you omit the parameter, Microsoft Entra Connect derives a sign-in hint from the connector configuration and opens an interactive sign-in prompt. This behavior applies to Set-ADSyncAADCompanyFeature, Set-ADSyncAADPasswordSyncState, Enable-ADSyncExportDeletionThreshold, Set-ADSyncScheduler, and Set-ADSyncDirSyncConfiguration.

The Select Containers dialog in Synchronization Service Manager is now read-only. You can still use the dialog to view the current selections. To make changes, use Customize synchronization options in the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard.
When you configure Seamless Single Sign-On by using the standalone PowerShell module, you must import ADSync.psd1 before AzureADSSO.psd1.
Updated the bundled SQL Server 2022 LocalDB from version 16.0.4250.1 to 16.0.4262.2.
Fixed an Application-Based Authentication certificate rotation issue that could remove the last usable application key during directory replica delays.

Fixed an issue where expanding a previously deselected domain on the Domain and OU filtering page could reselect the domain and enable synchronization for the entire domain after the wizard completed.
Fixed multiple security vulnerabilities in bundled third-party dependencies and hardened local temporary-file permissions and SharePoint connector profile-image downloads.

Microsoft Graph permissions have been added to Microsoft Entra Connect. If you use app-scoped Conditional Access policies, review policies targeting Microsoft.Azure.SyncFabric or Microsoft 365 Reporting Service.
Fixed an issue where installing or upgrading Microsoft Entra Connect with an existing ADSync database could fail with error 0xE0474352.
Fixed an issue where upgrading Microsoft Entra Connect didn't update an installed Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable version earlier than 14.41.
Fixed an issue where the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard could close during startup when the Windows PowerShell Transcription policy contained an invalid output directory.
Fixed an issue where Synchronization Service Manager could close unexpectedly when you opened Connector Properties and listed directory partitions.
Fixed an issue where Change Credentials didn't open for connector rows outside the visible area on configurations with many Active Directory connectors.

Enabling Pass-through Authentication through the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard might fail while registering the locally installed Microsoft Entra Connect Authentication Agent. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.92.0.

## Overview

Code to runtime gives you end-to-end visibility across the software development lifecycle (SDLC). Code to runtime helps you find the origin of an issue, assess its blast radius, and fix the issue at the source.

add: - Where the issue originated, such as in code or the build pipeline.
- Which intermediate stages are involved. These stages include the image in the registry and the CI/CD pipeline that was part of the deployment.
- How many assets are affected, so you can see the impact.
- Which actions you can take at each stage.
rem: 1. Where the issue originated (for example, in code or the build pipeline).

3. How many assets are affected, giving you visibility into the blast radius.
4. Which actions you can take at each stage.

add: - If you fix the issue only at runtime, it can reappear during the next deployment.
- Fixing the issue at the source prevents recurring regressions.
- Understanding the impact helps you plan rollouts and coordinate work.
- It helps you identify the owner for the fix.
rem: - Fixing only at runtime can cause the issue to reappear during the next deployment.

add: ## Understand the impact of the issue
Before taking action, open the **All impacted assets** grid for more information:

- The list shows the impacted assets from the same source. It includes assets in the cloud environment or code environment. Fixing the issue at the source can impact all the affected assets either by automated CI/CD processes or by manual deployment of new code.

- Filter the list based on your preferences. For example, filter runtime assets by Kubernetes namespace to assign the issue to a specific development team. You can also filter by relevant asset metadata, such as image tags and labels.
- When you select a line, the system shows more details for that instance of the issue.

add: Turning off Defender for Servers for a subscription in the Azure portal automatically offboards eligible servers from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Changing from Plan 2 to Plan 1 or moving a machine between subscriptions doesn't trigger automatic offboarding.
To start offboarding and verify the result:
1. In **Microsoft Defender for Cloud** in the Azure portal, identify the subscription where you want to turn off Defender for Servers.

2. Turn off the plan using the [plan-change procedure](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/tutorial-enable-servers-plan#disable-defender-for-servers-on-a-subscription). This is the only action required to initiate offboarding. The software automatically handles intent validation, MDE extension removal,
3. Allow processing to complete, and then verify the result. Offboarding can take up to one hour for large subscriptions. If machines are powered off, the software retries later.

#customer intent: As an IT admin, I want to rotate the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server key so that I can maintain security in my hybrid identity environment.
# Rotate the Kerberos server key for Microsoft Entra Kerberos

In hybrid identity environments, Microsoft Entra Kerberos uses a shared Kerberos server key between on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) and Microsoft Entra ID. This key encrypts and protects Ticket Granting Tickets (TGTs) issued by Microsoft Entra ID. This article shows you how to r

The key is stored on a dedicated Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object in on-premises Active Directory and securely published to Microsoft Entra ID. This object is logical, not a physical server, and functions like a read-only domain controller (RODC) for Kerberos trust.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams: New chat sections for muted and meeting chats
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Teams will introduce two new chat sections—Muted chats (enabled by default) and Meeting chats (disabled by default)—to organize conversations. Rollout starts mid-October 2026, completing by mid-November. Users can enable, disable, and reorder these sections; no admin action is required.

entries.title: Microsoft cancels auto-labeling for Azure Storage and Azure SQL after two years of preview
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft has decided not to proceed with auto-labeling for Azure Storage, Azure SQL, and other non-M365 workloads at this time. The feature would have allowed auto-labeling policies for various Azure and data services, but the rollout is paused, with future updates communicated via Message center.

entries.before: Updated 14 September 2026, pulling phase 1 forward from mid-October to early October 2026. Password-only users will be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor method, removing the prior requirement to register SMS or voice first. Phase 1 covers synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows and FIDO2 security keys; phase 2 adds Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, the Authenticator app passkey and Authenticator passwordless sign-in. Microsoft recommends reviewing Conditional Access policies related to security information registration and considering requiring MFA to register security information.
entries.after: Reported 14 September 2026: the MFA registration flow changes so a passkey or another passwordless method can be the first method a user registers, rolling out in phases from October 2026 to February 2027.

entries.before: Self-service password reset will require a registered authentication method from 5 October 2026, so users with none lose the reset path.
entries.after: Microsoft's post, last updated 4 August 2026, gives two dates. On 5 October 2026 the SSPR registration campaign begins prompting users and administrators to register authentication methods where the SSPR setting requires registration and they do not have enough. On 7 November 2026 enforcement begins: SSPR no longer accepts directory-sourced contact information (mobilePhone, businessPhone, otherMails) unless it was explicitly registered as an authentication method. Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD; rollout early to mid-November. Microsoft says about 86% of SSPR verifications already use registered methods.

General Availability rollout for Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD begins and completes in late September 2026.

entries.title: Microsoft withdrew the External ID credential management API reference four days after publishing it: customer passkey self-service goes back to the Graph FIDO2 provisioning APIs

entries.before: Microsoft published a new reference page on 2 October 2026 (entra-docs commit 75ba36fed9). The credential management API, at https://{tenant-subdomain}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant-id}/api/v1.0/me/..., lets a signed-in customer list and register passkeys; deletion is 'coming soon' and still goes through Microsoft Graph. It is a separate Microsoft-published resource, appId 6bf38b3c-a70f-49aa-a1d9-10e4cc74dde9, whose service principal must be created by hand until automatic provisioning is available. Accepted delegated permissions: Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.Read, Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Read, Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.Passkey.ReadWrite and Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite. The external-tenant passkey how-to now points here instead of the Graph FIDO2 provisioning APIs.
entries.after: entra-docs commit 9608dc10c3 of 6 October 2026, 'Revert passkey credential management documentation (#14532)', deletes the 587-line credential management API reference published on 2 October and redirects its address to the Microsoft Graph fido2AuthenticationMethod resource. The external-tenant passkey how-to, re-dated 6 October, now reads 'Use the FIDO2 provisioning APIs to build this into your app' where it read 'Use the credential management API to build this experience with low-privilege delegated permissions', and answers 'No' where it answered 'Yes' to whether signed-in customers can register their own passkeys with delegated permissions. The sample is described as 'administrator-controlled provisioning with high-privilege application permissions ... intended for testing only'. The same reference was removed once before, on 9 September. Whether the resource application 6bf38b3c-a70f-49aa-a1d9-10e4cc74dde9 and its Me.UserAuthenticationMethod.* permissions still exist in the service is not stated by Microsoft.

entries.before: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention wait-on-send policies, letting organizations require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for that evaluation to complete. This means sensitive information is inspected against organizational policy before messages leave the organization, with admins controlling the maximum wait time. General Availability rollout for Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD begins and completes in late September 2026.

entries.before: The legacy Microsoft Graph /security/alerts endpoint stops returning data on 15 October 2026, moved back from 31 August 2026; callers must migrate to /security/alerts_v2 and swap SecurityEvents.* permissions for SecurityAlert.*.
entries.after: Microsoft's migration article states: 'The legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API available through the /security/alerts endpoint is deprecated and will be retired on October 15, 2026', and 'After October 15, 2026, the legacy /security/alerts endpoint will stop returning data.' It adds that the alerts and incidents API at /security/alerts_v2 'is not a direct, one-to-one replacement': alerts from sources that are not integrated with Microsoft 365 Defender, 'such as a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that isn't connected to the Microsoft Defender portal, or standalone and tuned alerts', are not returned by the new API. The Graph what's-new page carries the line 'Updated the retirement date for the legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API from August 31, 2026 to October 15, 2026', read on 7 October 2026.

entries.before: Between the 29 September and the 5 October dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal (merill/microsoft-info 4f54a87 to 974a2dd, 23:16 UTC), application roles went from 748 to 760 and delegated scopes from 828 to 838, with nothing removed. The twelve new application roles are SynchronizationMetadata.Read.All, .Read.OwnedBy, .ReadWrite.All and .ReadWrite.OwnedBy; ContentHub-Catalog.Read.All, ContentHub-Installed.Read.All and ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All; CustomObject.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All; CustomObjectDefinition.Read.All, .ReadBasic.All and .ReadWrite.All. Ten of them also arrive as delegated scopes requiring admin consent; the two OwnedBy roles are application only. All are enabled, none is in the permissions reference, and all twelve had been in Microsoft's deployment map since September or earlier.
entries.after: Between the 29 September and the 5 October dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal (merill/microsoft-info 4f54a87 to 974a2dd, 23:16 UTC), application roles went from 748 to 760 and delegated scopes from 828 to 838, with nothing removed. The twelve new application roles are SynchronizationMetadata.Read.All, .Read.OwnedBy, .ReadWrite.All and .ReadWrite.OwnedBy; ContentHub-Catalog.Read.All, ContentHub-Installed.Read.All and ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All; CustomObject.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All; CustomObjectDefinition.Read.All, .ReadBasic.All and .ReadWrite.All. Ten of them also arrive as delegated scopes requiring admin consent; the two OwnedBy roles are application only. All are enabled, none is in the permissions reference, and all twelve had been in Microsoft's deployment map since September or earlier. Afternoon pass, 6 October: the next dump of the same service principal (merill/microsoft-info 531674a, 12:09 UTC) does not carry the twelve names and is byte-identical to the dumps of 29 September and 1 October, 748 application roles and 828 delegated scopes. One read holds them and the next does not, so treat them as rolling out and not as settled; the catalog entries are left as the morning wrote them until a third read decides. Read again on 7 October: the dump of 6 October 12:09 UTC (531674a) had gone back to 748 application roles and 828 delegated scopes without the twelve, and the next one, 6 October 21:48 UTC (9c21ffa), carries 760 and 838 again with all twelve names. Two of three consecutive dumps hold them, which is what a ring-by-ring deployment looks like from one replica.

entries.before: Microsoft's migration article states: 'The legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API available through the /security/alerts endpoint is deprecated and will be retired on October 15, 2026', and 'After October 15, 2026, the legacy /security/alerts endpoint will stop returning data.' It adds that the alerts and incidents API at /security/alerts_v2 'is not a direct, one-to-one replacement': alerts from sources that are not integrated with Microsoft 365 Defender, 'such as a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that isn't connected to the Microsoft Defender portal, or standalone and tuned alerts', are not returned by the new API. The Graph what's-new page carries the line 'Updated the retirement date for the legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API from August 31, 2026 to October 15, 2026', read on 7 October 2026.
entries.after: Microsoft's migration article states: 'The legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API available through the /security/alerts endpoint is deprecated and will be retired on October 15, 2026', and 'After October 15, 2026, the legacy /security/alerts endpoint will stop returning data.' It adds that the alerts and incidents API at /security/alerts_v2 'is not a direct, one-to-one replacement': alerts from sources that are not integrated with Microsoft 365 Defender, 'such as a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that isn't connected to the Microsoft Defender portal, or standalone and tuned alerts', are not returned by the new API. The Graph what's-new page carries the line 'Updated the retirement date for the legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API from August 31, 2026 to October 15, 2026', read on 7 October 2026. The public source of the article, synchronised on 8 October 2026 (commit 5a88c6f), adds a fifth gap: 'Intune-originated alerts aren't available through alerts_v2. Retrieve the relevant data through the Microsoft Graph Intune APIs', and for the low-signal Exchange Online events it now names Microsoft Purview Audit and Exchange Online Message Trace as the places to read them.

delta.what: Microsoft's Graph permissions reference documents 33 more permissions, among them the thirteen that delete users' authentication methods, four identity-diagnostic names and four Customer Lockbox names
delta.after: read for the first time today
delta.why: Every one of these names was already in this catalog, read from the service principal or from Microsoft's deployment map weeks before the page carried it, so nothing new became grantable today. What changed is that an approver can now look the name up, and that a consent review built from the documentation gains 33 rows it did not have. The delete-only family grants no read and no write, so a review that searches for ReadWrite on authentication methods still does not find it.

delta.what: Policy.ReadWrite.Recovery is now documented as an application permission too: the organization's recovery policy becomes writable without a signed-in user
delta.before: Application column '-'; delegated scope only, identifier 1e7a2f4c-e602-4b1b-9547-304dd65c4cc2
delta.after: Application identifier 795fc94d-3deb-4632-b1eb-e6d1a5f44918, admin consent Yes: 'Allows the application to read and update the organization's recovery policy without a signed-in user.'
delta.why: A permission an application can hold unattended is a different risk from one exercised on behalf of a signed-in administrator, and this one writes a tenant-wide policy. The reference is ahead of the service principal here, so the first tenant grant will come after a ring deployment, with no announcement (inferred from the two sources disagreeing).

delta.what: Microsoft now writes it down: an application with User.ReadWrite.All can update users who hold privileged admin roles
delta.after: read for the first time today
delta.why: This is the vendor's own statement of something tenants routinely under-rate: User.ReadWrite.All as an application role is not a help-desk permission. It is the sentence to quote when an integration asks for it.

delta.what: MailboxItem.ImportExport and MailboxItem.ImportExport.All are relabelled from 'backup and restore' to 'export and import' of mailbox items
delta.before: 'Allows the app to perform backup and restore for all mailbox items'
delta.after: 'Export and import all the users' mailbox items'
delta.why: The new label says what the role always allowed. An application role that exports every mailbox is the most direct mail-exfiltration grant Graph has, and any review note or detection that matches on the old display text no longer matches.

delta.what: Entra Kerberos gets one configuration guide: the key-rotation page is folded into it, with a stated rotation practice and a warning that only Set-AzureADKerberosServer may rotate the key
delta.after: read for the first time today
delta.why: Tenants that use cloud Kerberos trust for Windows Hello for Business or FIDO2 sign-in to on-premises resources carry a second krbtgt-class key that many krbtgt rotation runbooks do not touch. Microsoft now says in one place that it belongs on the same schedule and in the same incident-response step.

delta.what: Conditional Access baseline-scope enforcement: the page now speaks of the rollout in the past tense and adds a Graph query that lists the policies it affects
delta.before: 'Rollout of the enforcement model for baseline scopes begins on June 15, 2026.' and 'the enforcement is enabled automatically, over a period of approximately several weeks'
delta.after: 'Rollout of the enforcement model for baseline scopes began on June 15, 2026.' and 'the enforcement is enabled automatically'; a Graph query listing All-resources policies with exclusions is added
delta.why: Sign-ins that request only baseline scopes used to pass an All-resources policy that carried exclusions; with enforcement they must satisfy it. The page no longer describes that as upcoming, so an unexplained Conditional Access prompt or failure on such an application is now expected behaviour rather than a fault.

delta.what: RD Web Access stops rendering when browsers switch off XSLT; Microsoft publishes KB5130994 with workarounds
delta.after: read for the first time today
delta.why: For organisations that still publish RemoteApp or desktops through RD Web Access this is an outage driven by a browser update, not by a Windows patch, so it will not line up with a change window. Expect the workaround that reaches users first to be an older or unmanaged browser.

watchlist.state: Documented on 8 October 2026; grantable since August
watchlist.what: Microsoft's permissions reference now carries UserAuthenticationMethod.Delete.All and twelve per-method UserAuthMethod-*.Delete.All application permissions, each with admin consent required. For passkeys: 'Allows the application to delete passkey authentication methods of all users in your organization, without a signed-in user. This does not allow the app to read, create, or modify passkey authentication methods.'
watchlist.soc: Deleting the strong method is how an account is pushed back to a weaker one. These roles grant no read or write, so they hide from reviews that search for ReadWrite; alert on any grant of the thirteen identifiers.

watchlist.topic: Authenticated password change in My Sign-Ins
watchlist.state: Rollout from mid-October 2026, off by default
watchlist.what: MC1437671, revised 7 October 2026: a user with a passkey, FIDO2 security key or Windows Hello for Business can set a new password from My Sign-Ins without knowing the current one and without SSPR. General availability, Worldwide and GCC, begins in mid-October 2026. 'The setting is tenant-wide ... There is no per-user or per-group scoping.'
watchlist.soc: One strong credential becomes enough to replace the password on the same account, for every user or for none. Decide before the switch appears, and watch password changes that follow a fresh passkey registration.

watchlist.topic: System-preferred authentication and the registration campaign
watchlist.what: Microsoft removed the note that the Microsoft managed state 'affects both first-factor and multifactor authentication and is being gradually deployed to tenants through September 2026', and the note that the new registration campaign 'is expected to finish by the end of September 2026'. The commit is titled 'Remove completed system-preferred rollout note'.
watchlist.soc: Both behaviours are now documented as every tenant's. A tenant that does not show them has a configuration difference worth finding, not a rollout to wait for.

watchlist.what: Microsoft's own version-history page states that all synchronisation services in Entra Connect Sync stop working on 30 September 2026 for any server below 2.5.79.0. The current build is 2.6.92.0, released 23 September 2026 as a hotfix for a Pass-through Authentication agent registration failure introduced in 2.6.91.0; 2.6.91.0 itself, on 16 September, made phishing-resistant authentication generally available and on by default.
watchlist.soc: If a Connect server is below 2.5.79.0 on 1 October, hybrid identity stops syncing: no new accounts, no disables, no group changes. A leaver who is disabled on-premises stays enabled in the cloud. That is the failure mode to plan for, not the sync alert.

watchlist.what: Three beta properties on security/auditLogQuery - isRecordCountLimitExceeded, recordCountLimit and approximateReturnedRecordCount - say whether a completed query hit the per-search record limit. Before them, a truncated answer and a quiet day looked identical.
watchlist.soc: Every collector that pages the unified audit log through Graph has been unable to tell the two apart. Read the flag and alert on it; a hunt that silently loses rows is worse than a hunt that fails.

watchlist.what: MC1474104, published 18 September, sets the date: from 1 February 2027 SMS first-factor sign-in is retired for Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenants worldwide and in GCC. Existing configurations stop being honoured and the management surface is removed.
watchlist.soc: Any account that can still sign in with a phone number and an SMS code is a phishable first factor with a February deadline on it. Inventory SignInNoPassword usage now; the population is usually frontline and shared-device users, who are the hardest to move.

watchlist.what: MC1426371, last revised 15 September, is the parent post: passkeys become the default registration path and Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire. Its own first deadline, 1 September 2026, has passed.
watchlist.soc: Tenants that relied on Microsoft-provided telephony have two exits — move to phishing-resistant methods, or bring their own telephony provider — and the provider route has its own dates.

watchlist.what: Provider information opened on 18 September 2026; customer configuration opens 30 October 2026, ahead of the February 2027 retirement.
watchlist.soc: This is the only path that keeps telephony-based methods alive. A tenant that wants it has roughly three months to select and contract a provider.

watchlist.topic: Passkeys as the first registered method
watchlist.what: MC1450133 lets a user register a passkey or another passwordless method as their first multifactor method, rather than having to register a phone first.
watchlist.soc: Removes the step that forced every new user through a phone number. It also removes the assumption, common in detection rules, that a first registration event is a phone registration.

watchlist.what: MC1459133 extends passkey registration and sign-in to B2B guest users in the resource tenant.
watchlist.soc: Guest identities have been the weakest link in phishing-resistant rollouts because the home tenant controlled the method. This gives the resource tenant a lever it did not have.

watchlist.topic: System-preferred authentication on the first factor
watchlist.what: System-preferred authentication starts applying to the first factor, not just to multifactor prompts, from 30 September 2026.
watchlist.soc: The method a user is offered first changes without any policy edit on the tenant side. Expect help-desk volume and a shift in the method distribution in sign-in logs at the end of the month.

watchlist.topic: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening
watchlist.what: MC1471963 is the 30-day reminder: the October 2026 Windows security update turns on Enforcement mode for AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening, remediating insecure ACLs automatically to close CVE-2026-56155. Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 are not remediated automatically.
watchlist.soc: This writes to a Tier 0 object on the federation path. Use the remaining audit period to read the AD FS Admin event log and confirm nothing in the tenant depends on the loose ACL.

strategic.head: The permissions reference catches up in batches, weeks after the service
strategic.text: On 8 October Microsoft documented 33 Graph permissions in one commit; this catalog had held every one of them from the service principal or the deployment map, some since August. A consent process that treats the reference page as the list of what can be granted is weeks behind what can be granted, and one section, Policy.ReadWrite.Recovery, is now ahead of the service instead.

strategic.head: A directory role reaches Graph app role assignments through one Microsoft application
strategic.text: Tenant Governance Administrator is now documented with application-scoped operations, among them managing app role assignments for Microsoft Graph and delegated permission grants. They are written as prose rows, not as microsoft.directory actions, so role-definition scanners do not see them; expect more roles to be documented this way.

strategic.head: The legacy Graph security alerts API fails silently on 15 October
strategic.text: After 15 October /security/alerts returns no data rather than an error, and Microsoft states its replacement is not one-to-one: alerts from a Sentinel workspace that is not connected to the Defender portal do not appear in alerts_v2. An integration can look healthy and be empty.

strategic.head: Exchange Server received an out-of-cycle fix nine days after its September update
strategic.text: CVE-2026-96940 was added on 2 October 2026 as a V2 of the 24 September release, and the WSUS Scan Cab was re-issued the same evening to detect it. A patch process that closes the month once the September update is on will carry this exposure until November unless build numbers are compared.

strategic.head: Two exploited elevation-of-privilege bugs are still being edited three weeks after release
strategic.text: CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880 both carry Exploited: Yes in Microsoft's September document, and both were revised between 14 and 28 September — an acknowledgement on 15 September, an exploit-maturity vector on 16 September. One of them still has no CVSS base score at all. A queue sorted on severity will not show either of them at the top.

strategic.head: Permissions now reach the service principal weeks after the deployment map shows them
strategic.text: The twelve names that became grantable on 5 October had been in Microsoft's deployment map since 29 October 2025 (SynchronizationMetadata), 3 September (CustomObject) and 9 September 2026 (ContentHub), and are still absent from the permissions reference. The same order held on 22 September. A consent watch list built from documentation lags the service; one built from the deployment map leads it.

strategic.head: Microsoft's own Entra what's-new pages have stopped answering for 16-30 September
strategic.text: All eight official Entra what's-new and breaking-change pages were read in this run and every one of them is stale against a 16-30 September window: the consolidated feed's newest entry is June 2026, identity-platform breaking changes still ends at August 2024. The dated record for Entra in the 16-30 September period comes from Message Center and from the documentation git history, and the Sources tab says so per area.

strategic.head: A service principal is the identity with the least Conditional Access coverage, and an actor is now named for it
strategic.text: Storm-3168 uses agentic tooling on compromised service principals for cloud reconnaissance and credential access. Workload identities have no MFA, no user to call and, in most tenants, no Conditional Access policy — which is the gap the write-up documents rather than discovers.

kql.title: Who was granted an application role that deletes users' authentication methods
kql.why: graph-permref-33-documented-2026-10-08: Microsoft documented the thirteen delete-only authentication-method roles on 8 October 2026.
kql.desc: Lists every successful grant in the last 90 days of one of the thirteen application roles that delete users' authentication methods, with who granted it and to which service principal. The identifiers are the ones Microsoft's permissions reference printed on 8 October. An empty result is the expected one; any row outside a joiner-mover-leaver tool needs an owner. It needs Entra audit logs in a Log Analytics workspace, and the modifiedProperties layout should be confirmed on one known grant in your own tenant.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 9 Oct 2026 - grants of the authentication-method delete application roles
// AuditLogs columns verified against the schema page cited beside this query.
// The thirteen identifiers are the ones Microsoft's permissions reference printed on 8 Oct 2026.
let DeleteRoles = datatable(AppRoleId:string, Permission:string) [
  "712f5e0d-bc8d-4ae5-8242-cfb9a4921ed3", "UserAuthenticationMethod.Delete.All",
  "f0e9adfd-ed6b-45f5-b969-324a75286a39", "UserAuthMethod-Email.Delete.All",
  "7fa6d39e-1e4e-44be-bf9c-e8260b12e1f5", "UserAuthMethod-External.Delete.All",
  "9d8eb432-7ea3-491a-9ed7-e6361b308f08", "UserAuthMethod-HardwareOATH.Delete.All",
  "ae494ca6-9612-417a-972a-ef52efaf2de3", "UserAuthMethod-MicrosoftAuthApp.Delete.All",
  "9563fbd0-03a7-466e-8042-63d668b7d1a3", "UserAuthMethod-Passkey.Delete.All",
  "59f17651-8b6c-494e-a269-4ac582fbbca0", "UserAuthMethod-Phone.Delete.All",
  "bd760918-651f-4e67-b66f-8f614384dec2", "UserAuthMethod-PlatformCred.Delete.All",
  "e1c34213-26ac-400b-9548-a749f1b1a4e0", "UserAuthMethod-QR.Delete.All",
  "a71aecaf-82f1-47c5-ad0a-5e63503b928f", "UserAuthMethod-ResourceKey.Delete.All",
  "e5676e10-1a16-452b-ad10-71f54b755852", "UserAuthMethod-SoftwareOATH.Delete.All",
  "4f872e9d-d232-4ecd-ab9c-337cbdb184e5", "UserAuthMethod-TAP.Delete.All",
  "f3197110-aa7f-4acd-a0fd-71981ad68d42", "UserAuthMethod-WindowsHello.Delete.All"
];
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where OperationName == "Add app role assignment to service principal"
| where Result =~ "success"
| mv-expand Target = TargetResources
| mv-expand Prop = Target.modifiedProperties
| where tostring(Prop.displayName) == "AppRole.Id"
| extend AppRoleId = trim('"', tostring(Prop.newValue))
| join kind=inner DeleteRoles on AppRoleId
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)),
         GrantedTo = tostring(Target.displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, Permission, GrantedTo, Actor, CorrelationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

kql.title: Which applications still call the legacy Graph security alerts API, eight days before it stops answering
kql.desc: The legacy /security/alerts endpoint stops returning data after 15 October 2026, and a caller that is not migrated gets an empty answer rather than an error. This lists every application, service principal and user that called it in the last 14 days, with the call count and the last call; an empty result means nothing in the tenant depends on it. It needs Microsoft Graph activity logs in a Log Analytics workspace.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 7 Oct 2026 - which applications still call the legacy Graph security alerts API?
// Table and columns verified against the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs schema page cited beside this query.
// The legacy endpoint is /security/alerts; /security/alerts_v2 is its replacement and is excluded.
// Needs Microsoft Graph activity logs exported to a Log Analytics workspace (Entra diagnostic settings).
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RequestUri has "/security/alerts" and RequestUri !has "/security/alerts_v2"
| summarize Calls = count(),
            LastCall = max(TimeGenerated),
            Methods = make_set(RequestMethod, 5),
            StatusCodes = make_set(ResponseStatusCode, 10),
            SampleUri = take_any(RequestUri)
          by AppId, ServicePrincipalId, UserId, ApiVersion
| order by Calls desc

    "73fac914-e726-4af5-9a46-62f65f7b0a8b",
    "2ebdaf81-319a-4058-9cb1-7c2c20cda877",

kql.title: Who sends or receives .msix and .msixbundle attachments, before Outlook starts blocking them in November
kql.why: MC1488841: from early November 2026 .msix and .msixbundle are added to BlockedFileTypes in every OWA mailbox policy.
kql.desc: From early November 2026 Outlook on the web and new Outlook block .msix and .msixbundle attachments in every OWA mailbox policy. This lists who exchanged such attachments in the last 30 days, with file names and hashes, so that a business process that depends on them is found before the block and anything else is looked at as a delivery attempt.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 6 Oct 2026 - who sends or receives .msix and .msixbundle attachments before Outlook blocks them (MC1488841)
// Table and columns verified against the EmailAttachmentInfo schema page cited beside this query.
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".msix" or FileName endswith ".msixbundle"
| summarize Messages = dcount(NetworkMessageId), Files = make_set(FileName, 20), Hashes = make_set(SHA256, 20), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress
| order by Messages desc

kql.title: Who edits email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List today, before Security Operator loses that access in November
kql.why: MC1486293: from early November 2026 the Entra Security Operator role no longer maps to Security settings in Defender for Office 365 Unified RBAC.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 3 Oct 2026 - who changes MDO threat policies and Tenant Allow/Block List entries
// Columns verified against the CloudAppEvents schema page cited beside this query.
// ActionType values are Exchange Online cmdlet names; confirm them in your own tenant (inferred).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType has_any ("TenantAllowBlockListItems", "AntiPhishPolicy", "AntiPhishRule",
        "HostedContentFilterPolicy", "MalwareFilterPolicy", "SafeLinksPolicy", "SafeAttachmentPolicy")
| where ActionType startswith "New-" or ActionType startswith "Set-" or ActionType startswith "Remove-"
| summarize Changes = count(), Cmdlets = make_set(ActionType, 20), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId
| order by Changes desc

kql.title: Conditional Access policies that granted access on an unmanaged device claiming a mobile or macOS platform
kql.why: The device platform condition is unverified and spoofable through the user agent (Microsoft Learn, Conditional Access: Conditions).
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 30 Sep 2026 - platform-only Conditional Access grants on unmanaged devices
// Columns verified against the SigninLogs schema page cited beside this query.
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ResultType == "0"
| extend OS = tostring(DeviceDetail.operatingSystem),
         Managed = tostring(DeviceDetail.isManaged),
         Compliant = tostring(DeviceDetail.isCompliant)
| where OS has_any ("iOS", "Android", "MacOs", "Linux")
| where Managed != "true" and Compliant != "true"
| mv-expand CAP = ConditionalAccessPolicies
| where tostring(CAP.result) == "success"
| summarize SignIns = count(), Users = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
            Agents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 5)
            by Policy = tostring(CAP.displayName), OS
| order by SignIns desc

kql.title: Machine accounts that lost their domain trust after the 14 September out-of-band update
kql.why: The out-of-band update KB5129195 and KB5129194 carry a documented known issue: a domain-joined machine protected by Credential Guard can lose its Active Directory trust relationship because Machine Identity Isolation is now enforced. A host in that state stops satisfying device-based Conditional Access, so it looks like a compliance drift rather than a servicing fault. This query separates the two by pairing the update event with the trust failure on the same device.

kql.title: Service principal sign-ins with no interactive user, grouped the way Storm-3168 works
kql.why: The Storm-3168 write-up describes agentic tooling driving compromised service principals for cloud reconnaissance and credential access. A workload identity has no MFA and no sign-in risk, so the only signal is shape: a principal that suddenly reads far more than it used to, from an address range it has never used. This query gives the baseline and the break in one pass.

kql.title: Active Directory objects created by the Cloud Sync provisioning agent
kql.why: The 24 September preview lets Cloud Sync create users and groups inside on-premises AD DS. Until a rule knows which account does that, every one of those creations looks like an on-premises actor making directory objects. This query names the creator so the expected source can be excluded and everything else kept.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 28 Sep 2026 - who creates objects in AD now that Cloud Sync can
// Table and columns verified against the IdentityDirectoryEvents schema page cited beside this query.
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("User created", "Group created", "Computer created")
| extend Target = tostring(TargetAccountUpn), Actor = tostring(AccountUpn)
| summarize Created = count(), Objects = make_set(Target, 100), Kinds = make_set(ActionType, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by Actor, DestinationDeviceName
| order by Created desc

add: | **Anthropic Claude Compliance** | Anthropic Claude Compliance events collected using the Codeless Connector Framework by BlueVoyant. | `_Im_AgentEvent_AnthropicClaudeCompliance` | `true` |

Turning off Defender for Servers for a subscription in the Azure portal automatically offboards eligible servers from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Changing from Plan 2 to Plan 1 or moving a machine between subscriptions doesn't trigger automatic offboarding.
To start offboarding and verify the result:
1. In **Microsoft Defender for Cloud** in the Azure portal, identify the subscription where you want to turn off Defender for Servers.

2. Turn off the plan using the [plan-change procedure](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/tutorial-enable-servers-plan#disable-defender-for-servers-on-a-subscription). This is the only action required to initiate offboarding. The software automatically handles intent validation, MDE extension removal, and endpoint offboarding.
3. Allow processing to complete, and then verify the result. Offboarding can take up to one hour for large subscriptions. If machines are powered off, the software retries later.
Use the subscription's plan control to initiate offboarding, not deletion of the Azure environment connection.

Automatic offboarding disconnects the endpoint from its current Defender for Endpoint organization and stops EDR reporting to that organization. It doesn't uninstall the endpoint software or remove historical device records. Software or record presence alone doesn't indicate a failure, and the plan setting alone doesn't confirm that offboarding is complete. Manual endpoint offboarding or uninstall

If you turn the plan back on before offboarding completes, the offboarding and onboarding actions run asynchronously. Defender for Endpoint is onboarded again after a few hours. Turning the plan back on doesn't immediately cancel offboarding.

pages.name: Deploy Defender for Endpoint on Linux using golden images

add: ### Add the onboarding package to the golden image

You can include the tenant-specific onboarding package in the golden image so that every machine created from the image onboards to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint automatically when the Defender service starts. Each clone onboards directly, without waiting for a separate deployment or extension to run. This approach is useful for short-lived or autoscaled virtual machines.

Copy the onboarding file to the golden image **only while the `mdatp` service is stopped**. If the service is running when you add the onboarding file, the golden image virtual machine onboards immediately and creates device identity state. That state is then captured in the image and carried over to every clone, which might cause multiple machines to report as the same device in the Microsoft Defender portal.
- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is installed on the golden image virtual machine, as described in Step 1. Use a current, supported version of the package.
- You have access to the Microsoft Defender portal with permissions to download the onboarding package.
1. In the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com), go to **Settings** > **Endpoints** > **Device management** > **Onboarding**.
2. Select **Linux Server** as the operating system.
3. For **Deployment method**, select **Your preferred Linux configuration management tool**.
5. Extract the package. It contains the `mdatp_onboard.json` onboarding file.
## Handle hostname changes on cloned machines

Defender for Endpoint reads the machine's hostname when the `mdatp` service starts and uses it to represent the device in the Microsoft Defender portal. If the hostname changes after the service starts, Defender for Endpoint continues to report the machine with the temporary or template hostname and its associated device ID until the service restarts. When the `mdatp` service restarts, Defender for Endpoint assigns the machine a new device ID and reports it with the current hostname.

On machines created from a golden image, the final hostname is often set during first boot by a provisioning service, such as `cloud-init`, a cloud platform agent, or a custom startup script. These services can run at the same time as the `mdatp` service. If `mdatp` starts first, it picks up the hostname from the golden image instead of the clone's final hostname.
If the hostname is set by a service that can run at the same time as the `mdatp` service, make sure the hostname is stable before you start the `mdatp` service on the cloned machine.
### Start Defender only after the hostname is stable
1. **On the golden image**, after you stop the service, disable it so that it doesn't start automatically when a clone boots.
2. **On each cloned machine**, wait until the service that sets the hostname has finished and the hostname has its final value.
3. Enable and start the Defender service.
rem: ## Hostname Management
If the hostname of a Linux server is changed after successful deployment of Defender, then you must restart the `mdatp` service to ensure the new hostname is correctly recognized by product.

# Manage system settings with Endpoint Privilege Management - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn

With Microsoft Intune **Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM)** your organization's users can run as a standard user (without administrator rights) and complete tasks that require elevated privileges. For more information, see [EPM Overview](overview).

An *elevation system settings policy* lets Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) grant standard users access to specific Windows system settings that normally require administrator rights. This policy type supports *network settings*, which let a standard user change IPv4, IPv6, and DNS server values for the network adapters on their device.

Some everyday tasks, like changing an IP address or DNS server, require administrator rights. A standard user who tries to change these values in Windows is blocked by a User Account Control (UAC) prompt. With an elevation system settings policy, you let standard users make these specific changes through EPM, without granting broad administrator rights and without a separate app deployment.

A common scenario is a user who travels between sites. To connect a device at a new location, the user might need to set a static IP address or DNS server before the device is online. An elevation system settings policy lets the user make that change, even when the device is offline.

rem: # Customer intent: As an administrator, I want to access the known limitations for Global Secure Access in one place. This article gathers all known issues and limitations into a single reference point. Global Secure Access articles with a "known limitations" section point to this article.

add: The Global Secure Access client doesn't currently support secure DNS in its different versions, such as DNS over HTTPS (DoH), DNS over TLS (DoT), or DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC). The client for macOS bypasses Secure DNS to enforce fully qualified domain name (FQDN)-based tunneling through the traffic forwarding policy. You don't need to disable Secure DNS in the browser or macOS.
rem: If Secure DNS is enabled on the browser or in macOS and the DNS server supports Secure DNS, then the client doesn't tunnel traffic set to be acquired by FQDN. (Network traffic that's acquired by IP isn't affected and is tunneled according to the forwarding profile.) To mitigate the Secure DNS issue, disable Secure DNS, set a DNS server that doesn't support Secure DNS, or create rules based on IP.

### Foundational CSPM moves to opt-in model for new Azure subscriptions

Starting October 27, 2026, Foundational CSPM will move to an opt-in model and will no longer be enabled by default for new Azure subscriptions. This change gives you more control over how security posture management is configured for each new Azure subscription and is part of the transition of cloud security posture management to the Microsoft Defender portal.
Foundational CSPM will continue to be available at no cost and can be enabled at any time based on your organization's needs.
This change applies only to new Azure subscriptions. Existing Azure subscriptions keep their current configuration, and AWS and GCP environments aren't affected.
For more information, see [Opt in to Foundational CSPM](foundational-cspm-opt-in).
Important

add: :::image type="complex" source="media/secure-key-release-pattern-trusted-launch/defense-in-depth-layers.png" alt-text="Diagram of the concentric defense-in-depth layers protecting the asset, and which threat direction each layer defends." lightbox="media/secure-key-release-pattern-trusted-launch/defense-in-depth-layers.png":::

The protected asset sits at the core. Four concentric layers enclose it, from innermost to outermost: Layer 1, attestation-gated Secure Key Release, where vTPM measured-boot claims gate key release; Layer 2, a hardened image with dm-verity, a read-only root, and no SSH or agent; Layer 3, network isolation with private endpoints, no public egress, and deny assignments; and Layer 4 (optional, shown with a dashed border), Confidential Computing that provides host memory encryption. Layers 1 through 3 defend against threat direction A, the consumer or VM and subscription owner using run-command, disk snapshot and swap, serial console, and managed-identity theft. Layer 4 defends against threat direction B, the host or hypervisor reading guest memory.

add: :::image type="complex" source="media/secure-key-release-pattern-trusted-launch/runtime-attestation-flow.png" alt-text="Diagram of the runtime attestation and key-release flow between the consumer tenant and the publisher tenant.":::

The consumer tenant (untrusted operator) contains the Trusted Launch VM, which has Secure Boot, a vTPM, and a hardened image. The publisher tenant (which holds the trust anchors) contains Microsoft Azure Attestation and a Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM that holds the exportable key and release policy. The flow has four steps: (1) the VM sends an attestation request with vTPM evidence to Microsoft Azure Attestation; (2) Microsoft Azure Attestation returns a signed MAA token containing the secureboot and PCR claims to the VM; (3) the VM sends `POST /keys/{key}/release` with the MAA token to Key Vault; (4) Key Vault returns the key wrapped to the vTPM ephemeral key, or `AccessDenied` if the policy isn't satisfied.

add: ### Automatic VM Guest Patching support after VM restore
Automatic VM Guest Patching and Hotpatching support can be lost after restoring a virtual machine from backup, depending on the restore method used.
- **Original Location Restore (OLR):** Automatic VM Guest Patching support is retained because the original VM metadata, including image reference information, is preserved.

- **Alternate Location Restore (ALR):** Automatic VM Guest Patching support may be lost because the restore operation creates a new VM instance that doesn't retain the original image reference metadata. The restored VM may be treated as a custom image VM and may no longer qualify for Automatic VM Guest Patching or Hotpatching. The restored VM may be treated as a custom image VM. Because custom images aren't currently supported for Automatic VM Guest Patching, the VM may no longer qualify for Automatic VM Guest Patching or Hotpatching.
To preserve Automatic VM Guest Patching and Hotpatching support after a restore operation, use **Original Location Restore (OLR)** whenever possible.
